definition_zh: 分集的；片段式的；间歇发作的
definition_en: arranged or occurring as separate self-contained episodes rather than one continuous whole
core_image: 一本没有装订线的书，每一章单独成页，翻过一页前一页就合上
scene: 评论人称该剧结构松散。Critics called its structure episodic.
sceneCN: 这里 episodic 是「片段式的」（第 1 个义项：由各自独立的场景拼成）；句意：评论人称该剧结构是片段式的。

pos.zh: 分集的；片段式的；间歇发作的

senses.title: Built out of separate instalments
senses.definition: composed of episodes that each close before the next begins
senses.definitionCN: 由各自收尾的若干片段组合而成
senses.example: The novel is episodic rather than plotted.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是片段式的而非情节连贯的。
senses.why: Each instalment keeps its own edges, so the shape of the whole reads as a string of beads.
senses.whyCN: 每段自留边界，整体轮廓便读作一串珠子。

senses.title: Memory for personal scenes
senses.definition: relating to the recall of specific events placed in time and place
senses.definitionCN: 指对特定时空之下具体事件的回忆
senses.example: Patients lose episodic memory first.
senses.exampleCN: 患者最先丧失情景记忆。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word because such memories arrive as scenes, not as facts.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用了这个词，因为这类记忆以场景而非事实到来。

senses.title: Coming in attacks
senses.definition: occurring in distinct bursts with quiet intervals between
senses.definitionCN: 一阵一阵地发作，间歇期平静
senses.example: Doctors described an episodic fever.
senses.exampleCN: 医生描述了一种间歇性发热。
senses.why: Medicine took the narrative sense over, since a bout is a story with an end.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了叙事义，因为一次病发本就是一段有结尾的故事。

intro.en: Episodic hangs from episode, Greek epeisodion, the interlude between two choruses.
intro.cn: episodic 挂在 episode 之下，源头是希腊语 epeisodion，指两次合唱之间的插段。

items.en: Hodos names a road or way.
items.cn: hodos 指道路。

items.en: Epeisodion marks an episode inserted between choral songs.
items.cn: epeisodion 指合唱之间插入的一段。

items.en: Episode transcribes the Greek noun.
items.cn: 拉丁语 episode 转写希腊名词。

items.en: Episode enters English by way of French.
items.cn: episode 经法语进入英语。

items.en: Literary critics attach the adjectival ending.
items.cn: 十九世纪文学批评加上了形容词词尾。

items.en: Television and psychology both adopt the adjective.
items.cn: 二十世纪的电视业与心理学同时采用了该形容词。

note.en: Group one holds relatives of the Greek way and instalment; group two holds other adjectives of broken sequence.
note.cn: 第一组是希腊语「道路」与「插段」的亲族；第二组是其他表断续的形容词。

entries.definition: One instalment, or an incident set apart from routine.
entries.definitionCN: 一集，或从日常中划出的一件事。

entries.definition: Returning at intervals, closer to rhythm than to narrative.
entries.definitionCN: 按间隔复现，偏向节奏而非叙事。

entries.definition: Built on the same Greek word for a road, meaning orderly.
entries.definitionCN: 同出希腊语道路一词，意为有条理。

entries.definition: Made of brief unpublished stories, loosely like episodic.
entries.definitionCN: 由未刊小段故事组成，与片段式略近。

entries.definition: Consisting of incomplete parts rather than closed scenes.
entries.definitionCN: 由不完整部分构成，而非闭合场景。

entries.definition: Lacking transitions between one part and the next.
entries.definitionCN: 部分之间缺少过渡。

entries.definition: Pausing and resuming, used chiefly of processes.
entries.definitionCN: 停停续续，多修饰过程。

entries.definition: Published in successive parts, often still one story.
entries.definitionCN: 分期刊载，仍常为同一故事。

normalIntro.en: Episodic stresses that the parts stand alone; serial stresses that they follow one another.
normalIntro.cn: episodic 强调各段独立，serial 强调前后相续。

normal.en: It is neutral in criticism but often implies weak overall plot.
normal.cn: 在批评中语气中性，但常暗示整体情节薄弱。

normal.en: Episodic memory is a fixed term in psychology.
normal.cn: episodic memory 是心理学固定术语。

normal.en: Pair with structure, format, pattern, series.
normal.cn: 搭配 structure、format、pattern、series。

normal.en: In medicine it means attacks with clear gaps.
normal.cn: 医学上指发作之间有明显空隙。

normal.en: Avoid it for a story that merely has chapters.
normal.cn: 仅有章节的故事不必用这个词。

abstract.en: Picture a necklace of separate glass beads.
abstract.cn: 想象一串彼此独立的玻璃珠。

abstract.en: Imagine a television series you can start at any episode.
abstract.cn: 想象一部从任意一集都能入戏的电视剧。

abstract.en: Think of a fever that lights and goes out like a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想想一盏点亮又熄灭的灯那样的一阵发热。

examples.en: Her early career was episodic, three months here, four there.
examples.cn: 她的早期生涯断断续续，这儿三个月，那儿四个月。

examples.en: Episodic delivery lets writers restart without recap.
examples.cn: 分集播出让编剧无需前情回顾即可重启。

examples.en: The diary stays episodic, one weather entry per day.
examples.cn: 这本日记保持片段式，每天一条天气记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: “爱批散”——爱把整块材料批成散段，一段自成一体，所以 episodic 是分集的、片段式的；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 epi-（在……之上）＋ hodos（路）→ epeisodion（合唱之间插入的一段）→ episode ＋ 词尾 -ic → episodic，核心义「一段一段自成起讫」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective describes narrative shape, a memory system, and a pattern of attacks.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词描述叙事形态、一种记忆系统，以及发作的节律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: closed scenes set side by side with visible gaps between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：各自闭合的场景并列摆放，中间留有可见的空隙。

branches.en: Storytelling hands each scene its own door.
branches.cn: 叙事为每一场戏留一扇门。

branches.en: Memory files the day by scene rather than by rule.
branches.cn: 记忆按场景而非按规则归档。

branches.en: The body opens and closes its attacks like chapters.
branches.cn: 身体像翻章一样开启并结束发作。

branches.en: Both divide experience into packaged units.
branches.cn: 两者都把体验打包成单元。

branches.en: Both depend on recall of when a thing happened.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖对何时发生的回忆。

intro.en: A prefix of position, a noun of road, and an adjectival ending stack in order.
intro.cn: 表位置的前缀、表道路的名词与形容词词尾依次叠起。

latinIntro.en: Greek hodos is a way, epeisodion an interlude, periodos a circuit.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 hodos 表道路，epeisodion 表插段，periodos 表环绕。

items.example: A cousin built on the same hodos.
items.exampleCN: 同一 hodos 上的表亲词。
meta- 加 hodos 构成 method。

definition_zh: 成为……的典型；概括；提炼
definition_en: to be a perfect example of something, or to state something in a very short form
core_image: 一座城市把所有时代的矛盾收进同一条街，走过这一条就算走完整座城
scene: 这条街浓缩了整座老城的心事。This street epitomises the old town.
sceneCN: 这里 epitomise 是「成为……的典型；概括」（第 1 个义项：以一小段呈现整体）；句意：这条街是整座老城的缩影。

senses.title: To sum up a whole in one instance
senses.definition: to present an entire quality or class in a single clear example
senses.definitionCN: 用一个清晰的例子呈现整种性质或整类事物
senses.example: His silence epitomised the mood.
senses.exampleCN: 他的沉默正是那种心情的缩影。
senses.why: The Greek noun named an abstract copy, so one case could stand for the class.
senses.whyCN: 希腊名词指抽象的抄本，因此一个个例便可代表整类。

senses.title: To abridge a text
senses.definition: to restate a longer work in the fewest usable words
senses.definitionCN: 用最少的可用文字复述较长作品
senses.example: The editor epitomised the report.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把报告压缩成摘要。
senses.why: Older rhetoric kept the abstracting sense that still lives in epitome.
senses.whyCN: 早期修辞学保留了摘要义，该义至今活在名词 epitome 里。

senses.title: To cut short
senses.definition: a rare use meaning to reduce a thing to its essentials
senses.definitionCN: 罕见用法，指把事物削减到仅剩精要
senses.example: Reform epitomised the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 改革把委员会缩减到最小规模。
senses.why: A literal sense from the Greek verb, to cut short, survives only on paper.
senses.whyCN: 来自希腊动词的字面义「切短」如今仅存于书面。

intro.en: Epitomise comes through Latin epitomizare from Greek epitomizein, to make an abstract, from epitome, an abridgement.
intro.cn: epitomise 经拉丁语 epitomizare 而来，源自希腊语 epitomizein「作摘要」，其基础是 epitome「节略本」。

items.en: Temnein means to cut.
items.cn: temnein 意为切。

items.en: Epitome names a cutting short, then a summary.
items.cn: epitome 先指切短，再指摘要。

items.en: Epitoma and epitomizare carry the noun into scholarship.
items.cn: epitoma 与 epitomizare 把名词带进学术。

items.en: Epitomiser supplies the modern verb shape.
items.cn: epitomiser 提供现代动词形式。

items.en: English first records the verb in a learned tone.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语首见该动词，语气书面。

items.en: Review writing makes it the praise of a perfect example.
items.cn: 十九世纪书评把它变成对典型之例的赞美。

note.en: Group one holds the temnein cutting family; group two holds other verbs of typifying and condensing.
note.cn: 第一组是 temnein 这一表切割的词族；第二组是其他表典型化与浓缩的动词。

entries.definition: The summary, or the perfect example itself.
entries.definitionCN: 摘要，或典型范例本身。

entries.definition: A division cut in two, from the Greek temnein.
entries.definitionCN: 切成两半的分立，出自希腊语 temnein。

entries.definition: To dissect, built on the same verb of cutting.
entries.definitionCN: 剖解分析，基于同一表切割的动词。

entries.definition: Greek atomos means the indivisible, sharing temnein.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 atomos 指不可分，同出 temnein。

entries.definition: To be a regular instance of a type.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某种类型的常态实例。

entries.definition: To illustrate by a case, without claiming perfection.
entries.definitionCN: 举例说明，不宣称完美无缺。

entries.definition: The plain way to compress a whole into a few words.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体压成数语的朴素说法。

entries.definition: To put into a small compass, close to the abridging sense.
entries.definitionCN: 纳入小范围，接近节略之义。

normalIntro.en: Epitomise is the British spelling; the American form drops the s for a z.
normalIntro.cn: epitomise 是英式拼写，美式把 s 换成 z。

normal.en: Its object is an abstract: a mood, an era, a virtue.
normal.cn: 宾语多为抽象物：心情、时代、美德。

normal.en: Use the passive with in: the age was epitomised in one song.
normal.cn: 与 in 连用表被动：一个时代浓缩在一首歌里。

normal.en: Do not epitomise a person; epitomise what they stand for.
normal.cn: 不要说概括某人，要概括其所代表之物。

normal.en: Reviewers favour it, engineers rarely use it.
normal.cn: 书评人偏爱此词，工程写作少用。

normal.en: The noun epitome keeps the same two senses.
normal.cn: 名词 epitome 保留同样的两个义项。

abstract.en: Picture a single street holding every argument of a whole city.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街道容下一座城市的所有争执。

abstract.en: Imagine scissors cutting a thick book down to one page.
abstract.cn: 想象剪刀把一本厚书裁到只剩一页。

abstract.en: Think of one photograph that ends a long debate about an era.
abstract.cn: 想想一张照片便终结了关于一个时代的长辩。

examples.en: One gesture epitomised her whole method.
examples.cn: 一个动作概括了她的全部方法。

examples.en: The slogan epitomises decades of patient research.
examples.cn: 这句口号浓缩了数十年沉静的研究。

examples.en: Critics felt the film epitomised the decade's anxiety.
examples.cn: 批评者认为该片是十年不安的典型写照。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一劈题眉子」——一刀劈下只留下题目最上面那一道眉，所以 epitomise 是提炼、概括成典型；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 epi-（在上）＋ temnein（切）→ epitome（切短之物、摘要）→ 拉丁语 epitomizare → 法语 epitomiser → 英语 epitomise，核心义「一刀切到只剩精要」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb moves from standing as a perfect example, to abridging a text, to a bookish sense of cutting short.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从充当典型范例，到节略文本，再到书卷气的截短之义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one cut leaves the smallest piece that still shows the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一刀切下，留下的最小一片仍能显出全貌。

branches.en: The chosen instance carries the class.
branches.cn: 所选个例承载整类。

branches.en: The text is trimmed to usable length.
branches.cn: 文本被修剪到可用长度。

branches.en: A literal cutting sense lingers in old prose.
branches.cn: 字面的切割义留在早期文本中。

branches.en: Both begin from the image of the blade.
branches.cn: 两者都从刀的意象出发。

branches.en: Both mean making a thing shorter on purpose.
branches.cn: 两者都指有意使对象变短。

intro.en: A prefix of position, a stem of cutting, and a verbal ending assemble the word.
intro.cn: 表位置的前缀、表切割的词干与动词词尾装配成本词。

latinIntro.en: Greek temnein is to cut, Latin sectare is to cut too, and tomus is a section.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 temnein 表切，拉丁语 sectare 亦表切，tomus 表章节。

items.example: Epi- marks the cut from above.
items.exampleCN: epi- 标示自上而下的切。

items.example: The same stem yields the noun.
The ending forms the British verb.

items.exampleCN: 在评论性过去时中常见。

definition_zh: 纪元；新时代；地质世
definition_en: a period of time marking the start of a new and distinctive development, or a fixed division of geologic time
core_image: 地层剖面上一条白线，线下的岩层属于另一个世界，线上的世界刚刚出生
scene: 印刷术开启了新的知识时代。Printing opened a new epoch of knowledge.
sceneCN: 这里 epoch 是「新时代；纪元」（第 1 个义项：以重大变化划界的时期）；句意：印刷术开启了知识的新纪元。

derivatives.zh: 划时代的；属某一纪元的

senses.title: An era reckoned from one event
senses.definition: a stretch of history dated from a turning point that changed its character
senses.definitionCN: 以改变性质的转折点为起点计算的一段历史
senses.example: Steam began an epoch.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸汽机开启了一个时代。
senses.why: The Greek noun meant a fixed point from which reckoning starts, and the point defines the span.
senses.whyCN: 希腊名词指计算的起点，起点定义了整段跨度。

senses.title: A formal division of geologic time
senses.definition: a unit of geologic time, a subdivision of a period, marked by distinct strata
senses.definitionCN: 地质年代单位，为「纪」之下的 subdivision，以地层特征为界
senses.example: The Pleistocene epoch left moraines.
senses.exampleCN: 更新世留下了冰碛垄。
senses.why: Stratigraphy borrowed the word and gave it boundaries readable in rock.
senses.whyCN: 地层学借用该词，并给它以岩层可读的界线。

senses.title: A computed reference instant
senses.definition: the instant chosen as zero for an astronomical or orbital calculation
senses.definitionCN: 天文或轨道计算中选作零点的时刻
senses.example: The orbit uses a midnight epoch.
senses.exampleCN: 该轨道以子夜为历元。
senses.why: Astronomy keeps the oldest arithmetic sense, the starting date of a table.
senses.whyCN: 天文学保留最古老的算术义，即数表的起算日期。

intro.en: Epoch is Greek epokhe, a stopping or holding, from epi- upon plus ekhein to hold.
intro.cn: epoch 出自希腊语 epokhe，意为停住或按住，由 epi-「在上」加 ekhein「持」构成。

items.en: Ekhein means to hold.
items.cn: ekhein 意为持握。

items.en: Epokhe meant a cessation, and in philosophy a suspension of judgment.
items.cn: epokhe 指中止，在哲学中指悬判断。

items.en: Astronomers used it for the date from which computation begins.
items.cn: 天文学家用它指计算开始的日期。

items.en: Epocha carries the term into scholarly Latin.
items.cn: epocha 把该词带入学术拉丁语。

items.en: English records epoch in chronology and astronomy.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语在年代学与天文中记录该词。

items.en: Geology adopts it for a subdivision of time in rock.
items.cn: 十九世纪地质学用它指岩层中的时间单位。

note.en: Group one holds the ekhein holding family and the adjective; group two holds other words for long spans.
note.cn: 第一组是 ekhein 这一表持握的词族与形容词；第二组是其他表长时段的词。

entries.definition: Characterising an age rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容一个时代的特征，而非命名。

entries.definition: A short self-contained piece, not a vast span.
entries.definitionCN: 短小自足的一片段，而非漫长时段。

entries.definition: Lasting a day, on the Greek hēmera.
entries.definitionCN: 仅持续一日，出自希腊语 hēmera。

entries.definition: A circle upon a circle in older astronomy.
entries.definitionCN: 旧天文学中圆上的另一个圆。

entries.definition: The common word for a period with a character of its own.
entries.definitionCN: 表自有面貌的时期，日常通用。

entries.definition: The shortest and broadest term for a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 最简短宽泛的长时间说法。

entries.definition: A stretch with set edges, plainer and vaguer than epoch.
entries.definitionCN: 有确定边界的时段，比 epoch 更平实也更模糊。

entries.definition: One released part of a series, not a measure of deep time.
entries.definitionCN: 系列中发布的一份，不是深时单位。

normalIntro.en: Epoch is heavier than era and is the technical unit in geology.
normalIntro.cn: epoch 比 era 语气更重，且是地质学的技术单位。

normal.en: Say a new epoch, not an epoch of new.
normal.cn: 说 a new epoch，不说 an epoch of new。

normal.en: Stress falls on the first syllable in British speech.
normal.cn: 英式读音重音在第一音节。

normal.en: Geologists rank it below period and above age.
normal.cn: 地质序列中它低于「纪」而高于期。

normal.en: Epochal modifies change, discovery, shift.
normal.cn: 形容词 epochal 修饰变化、发现、转折。

normal.en: Do not use it for a decade with no turning point.
normal.cn: 没有转折点的十年不宜用它。

abstract.en: Picture a white line painted across a cliff face of rock.
abstract.cn: 想象崖壁上横画的一条白线。

abstract.en: Imagine a calendar whose page one begins with one invention.
abstract.cn: 想象一本从一项发明开始翻页的历书。

abstract.en: Think of a stopwatch pressed at the moment everything changes.
abstract.cn: 想想万物改变那一刻被按下的秒表。

examples.en: The telescope opened an epoch in astronomy.
examples.cn: 望远镜开启了天文学的一个纪元。

examples.en: Two epochs are debated as the start of human impact.
examples.cn: 人类影响的起点有两个时代之争。

examples.en: Its epochal status is rarely questioned now.
examples.cn: 它划时代的地位如今很少被质疑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一破壳」——一枚蛋破壳后世界便不再相同，所以 epoch 是纪元、划时代的开端；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 epi-（在上）＋ ekhein（持、停）→ epokhe（停住、起算点）→ 拉丁语 epocha → 英语 epoch，核心义「把时间按住、从此重新起算的那个点」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun serves common history, geologic measurement, and astronomical reckoning.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词服务于日常历史、地质计量与天文起算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a point where the clock is stopped and restarted from one.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟被按停，随后从一数重新走起的那个点。

branches.en: History takes the restart as its chapter mark.
branches.cn: 历史把重启当作章节记号。

branches.en: Rock records the boundary without naming it.
branches.cn: 岩层记下界线却不命名。

branches.en: Calculation needs a zero instant to count from.
branches.cn: 计算需要一个零点时刻起算。

branches.en: Both depend on a chosen starting point.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖被选定的起点。

branches.en: Both are technical uses with fixed rules.
branches.cn: 两者都是有确定规则的专门用法。

intro.en: A prefix of position joins a verb of holding, and the result names a stop that starts counting.
intro.cn: 表位置的前缀接上表持握的动词，其结果命名那个让计数开始的停顿。

latinIntro.en: Greek ekhein is to hold, schēma a shape held, and epocha the Latin borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 ekhein 表持握，schēma 表所持之形，epocha 为拉丁借词。

items.exampleCN: 词干在 e-pokh-e 中缩短。
同一持握词干，意义不同。

items.example: A cousin about time rather than holding.
items.exampleCN: 时间而非持握上的表亲词。

definition_zh: 相等的；平等的；同等的人；等于
definition_en: the same in amount, value, or status, or to be the same as something
core_image: 天平两端放着同样重的东西，横杆保持水平
scene: 两根绳子长度相同，承受的重量也一样。The two ropes are equal in length and strength.
sceneCN: 这里 equal 是「相等的」（第 1 个义项：在数量或程度上相同）；句意：两根绳子的长度和强度都相同。

senses.title: The same in amount or degree
senses.definition: having the same size, amount, value, or level as something else
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量、价值或水平上与他人或他物相同
senses.example: Cut the cake into eight equal pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 把蛋糕切成八块大小相等的份。
senses.why: Latin aequalis means level or even, so equal first describes things that balance perfectly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aequalis 意为水平、均匀，所以 equal 首先描述完全平衡的事物。

senses.title: Having the same rights or status
senses.definition: having the same rights, opportunities, or treatment as others
senses.definitionCN: 与其他人拥有相同的权利、机会或待遇
senses.example: Every citizen deserves equal treatment under the law.
senses.exampleCN: 每位公民在法律面前都应得到平等对待。
senses.why: The idea of an even balance extends from weights and amounts to people and their rights.
senses.whyCN: 「平衡」的概念从重量和数量扩展到人及其权利。

senses.title: A person of the same rank
senses.definition: a person who has the same ability, rank, or status as another
senses.definitionCN: 能力、地位或身份与另一人相同的人
senses.example: She treats her students as her equals.
senses.exampleCN: 她把学生当作与自己平等的人。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for someone who stands on the same level.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，指站在同一水平上的人。

senses.title: To be the same as
senses.definition: to be the same in amount or value as something, or to match it
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或价值上等同于某物，或与之匹敌
senses.example: Two plus three equals five.
senses.exampleCN: 二加三等于五。
senses.why: The verb turns the balanced relation into an action of matching.
senses.whyCN: 动词把平衡关系转化为「相配、等同」的动作。

intro.en: Equal comes from Latin aequalis, uniform or even, from aequus, level or fair.
intro.cn: equal 来自拉丁语 aequalis（均匀、相等），源于 aequus（平的、公平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level, even, or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、均匀的、公平的。

items.en: Aequalis means uniform or of the same age.
items.cn: aequalis 意为均匀的或同年的。

items.en: Equal carries the sense of even and alike.
items.cn: equal 带有「平、相同」的含义。

items.en: Equal covers amounts and the rights of people.
items.cn: 中古英语 equal 涵盖数量与人的权利。

items.en: Modern English adds the noun for a person of the same rank.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了表示同等之人的名词用法。

note.en: Equal is a balance word with a large family and a set of near words for sameness.
note.cn: equal 是表示「平衡」的词，拥有庞大词族，并与表示相同的一组词相邻。

entries.definition: in an equal way
entries.definitionCN: 同样地；平等地

entries.definition: the state of being equal
entries.definitionCN: 平等；相等

entries.definition: to treat as equal
entries.definitionCN: 等同；使相等

entries.definition: not different
entries.definitionCN: 相同的

entries.definition: exactly the same
entries.definitionCN: 完全相同的

entries.definition: level or balanced
entries.definitionCN: 平的；均衡的

normalIntro.en: Equal comes from a level root: two sides of a scale sitting perfectly even.
normalIntro.cn: equal 来自「水平」的词根：天平两边完全齐平。

normal.en: Equal parts means every part is the same size.
normal.cn: equal parts 指每一份大小相同。

normal.en: Equal rights means the same rights for everyone.
normal.cn: equal rights 指人人拥有相同权利。

normal.en: The verb equals appears in arithmetic.
normal.cn: 动词 equals 出现在算术中。

normal.en: Equality is the noun for the equal state.
normal.cn: equality 是表示平等状态的名词。

normal.en: Compare identical: identical is stricter, equal allows different forms of the same value.
normal.cn: 对比 identical：identical 更严格，equal 允许同一价值的不同形式。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with two identical weights.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平两端放着相同的砝码。

abstract.en: Imagine eight cake slices cut by a careful hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手仔细切出八块相同的蛋糕。

abstract.en: Think of two runners crossing a line at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者同时冲过终点线。

examples.en: The two teams finished with equal scores.
examples.cn: 两支队伍最终得分相同。

examples.en: The law promises equal pay for equal work.
examples.cn: 法律承诺同工同酬。

examples.en: One kilometer equals a thousand meters.
examples.cn: 一公里等于一千米。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e + qual」——两边一样平，就是相等；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的、公平的）→ aequalis（均匀的）→ 古法语 equal → 英语 equal，核心义「两端齐平、彼此相同」。

sensesIntro.en: Equal starts with even amounts, extends to fair treatment, then to a person of the same standing, and finally to the verb of matching.
sensesIntro.cn: equal 从数量相等开始，扩展到公平对待，再指地位相同的人，最后成为表示「等于」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale perfectly level on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两边完全水平。

branches.en: Even amount is the basic measurable sense.
branches.cn: 数量相等是基本的可测量义项。

branches.en: Fair treatment extends balance to rights.
branches.cn: 公平对待把平衡扩展到权利。

branches.en: A peer is a person on the same level.
branches.cn: 同等之人是站在同一水平上的人。

branches.en: The verb states that two things match.
branches.cn: 动词陈述两事物彼此相等。

branches.en: Equal shares and equal rights both rest on the same balance.
branches.cn: 均分与平权都建立在同一种平衡之上。

intro.en: Equal is a Latin fairness word, and English builds equality, equally, and equate around it.
intro.cn: equal 是拉丁语中表示公平的词，英语围绕它构成 equality、equally 与 equate。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level and fair, and aequalis means even or uniform.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的、公平的，aequalis 意为均匀的。

items.example: Equally means in the same measure.

items.exampleCN: un- 在 unequal 中否定 equal。

definition_zh: 使相等；等同看待；折合
definition_en: to consider two things as the same, or to make amounts equal or interchangeable
core_image: 两架天平被人为放上同样的砝码，一根线把两个原本不同的词钉在同一格上
scene: 报表把工时直接折成成本。Reports equate hours with cost.
sceneCN: 这里 equate 是「等同看待；使相等」（第 1 个义项：把两者摆成等价）；句意：报表把工时与成本等同。

collocations.zh: 把 A 与 B 等同

senses.title: To treat two things as one in value
senses.definition: to regard different notions as if they carried the same meaning or worth
senses.definitionCN: 把不同观念视作含义或价值相同
senses.example: Polls equate attention with support.
senses.exampleCN: 民调把关注度等同于支持度。
senses.why: The Latin stem is levelness itself, so the verb lays two things on one scale.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干本义即平坦均等，动词因而把两物放上同一杆秤。

senses.title: To make amounts numerically equal
senses.definition: to set values equal, or to convert one into the other at a fixed rate
senses.definitionCN: 把数值设为相等，或按固定比率把一种换算成另一种
senses.example: The table equates units across currencies.
senses.exampleCN: 该表按不同货币折算单位。
senses.why: Accounting and science took the word for the arithmetic operation itself.
senses.whyCN: 会计与科学把该词用作算术运算本身。

senses.title: To match by comparison
senses.definition: a use in which one thing is held alongside another as its counterpart
senses.definitionCN: 把一物与另一物并置，视为与之相当的对应者
senses.example: Commentators equated the runner's grit.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者把跑者的韧劲拿来比配他人。
senses.why: Rhetoric borrows the equalising move to draw likeness between unlike things.
senses.whyCN: 修辞借这种拉平之举在异类之间描出相似。

intro.en: Equate is a modern verb drawn back from equation, whose Latin source aequatus means made level.
intro.cn: equate 是从 equation 逆推而来的晚近动词，其拉丁源头 aequatus 意为被弄平。

items.en: Aequus means level or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平坦、公正。

items.en: Aequare means to make level.
items.cn: aequare 意为使平坦。

items.en: Aequatus, made equal, feeds the noun equation.
items.cn: aequatus（被弄平）滋养了名词 equation。

items.en: English keeps equation before making a verb of it.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语先有 equation，再由此造出动词。

items.en: Equate appears in mathematical and commercial prose.
items.cn: 十九世纪 equate 见于数学与商务文本。

items.en: Social commentary adopts it for dubious identifications.
items.cn: 二十世纪社会评论用它指可疑的画等号。

note.en: Group one holds the aequus family; group two holds other verbs of making or claiming sameness.
note.cn: 第一组是 aequus 词族；第二组是其他表建立或声称同一性的动词。

entries.definition: The statement of equality, and the abstract act of equating.
entries.definitionCN: 等式，以及等同之举的抽象名词。

entries.definition: To bring things to the same level or score.
entries.definitionCN: 使达到同一水平或比分。

entries.definition: To speak on both sides of a question, evading a clear answer.
entries.definitionCN: 两可其辞，回避明确回答。

entries.definition: Level with what a task requires, from ad- plus aequus.
entries.definitionCN: 与任务所需持平，出自 ad- 加 aequus。

entries.definition: To treat one thing as the same as another.
entries.definitionCN: 把一物当作与另一物相同。

entries.definition: To set side by side as comparable.
entries.definitionCN: 并置以显可比。

entries.definition: To hold quantities in equilibrium.
entries.definitionCN: 使数量保持均势。

entries.definition: To correspond or pair as equal in kind.
entries.definitionCN: 相配或在同类中等量齐观。

normalIntro.en: Equate with or to is usual; equate as is the older bookish pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 常用 equate with 或 equate to，equate as 是较早的书面格式。

normal.en: In argument it warns of a false equivalence.
normal.cn: 在论辩中它警示错误的画等号。

normal.en: In finance it converts one unit into another.
normal.cn: 在财经中它把一种单位折算成另一种。

normal.en: Passive is common: salaries were equated with effort.
normal.cn: 被动式常见：薪水曾被视为与努力相等。

normal.en: Avoid it where analogy, not equality, is meant.
normal.cn: 本意是类比而非等同时不要用。

normal.en: Its noun is equation, not equatement.
normal.cn: 其名词为 equation，而非 equatement。

abstract.en: Picture a scale made honest only by adding weights.
abstract.cn: 想象一架只有加码才见公平的天平。

abstract.en: Imagine two coins stamped from one die.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚由同一印模压出的硬币。

abstract.en: Think of a spreadsheet cell that forces two columns to agree.
abstract.cn: 想想电子表格里迫使两列一致的那个单元格。

examples.en: Do not equate silence with consent.
examples.cn: 不要把沉默等同于同意。

examples.en: The schedule equates a night shift with extra pay.
examples.cn: 排班表把夜班折成额外工资。

examples.en: Historians equated the coin with a trade route.
examples.cn: 史家把这枚硬币与一条商路挂起等号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一快他特」——一样快的两件东西被特意指成一类，所以 equate 是使相等、等同看待；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平坦、均等）→ aequare（使平）→ aequatus（被弄平）→ 名词 equation → 逆构动词 equate，核心义「把两样东西放到同一水平线上」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb covers a claim of sameness, an arithmetic conversion, and a rhetorical pairing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词涵盖同一性的断言、算术的折算与修辞的并置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two uneven things brought to one line on the same scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样不齐之物被放上同一杆秤的同一条线。

branches.en: Judgment declares unlike things alike.
branches.cn: 判断把不同类之物宣称为同类。

branches.en: Arithmetic carries the claim into numbers.
branches.cn: 算术把这一宣称带进数字。

branches.en: Rhetoric pairs things for effect, not for proof.
branches.cn: 修辞为一效果而非一论证而并置两物。

branches.en: Both rest on comparison rather than measurement.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖比较而非计量。

branches.en: Both invite the charge of a false equivalence.
branches.cn: 两者都会招来虚假等号之责。

intro.en: A level adjective becomes a causative verb and then, in English, a back-formed verb with a fresh ending.
intro.cn: 表平坦的形容词先变为使动动词，再在英语里被逆构为带新词尾的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus is level, aequare to level, and aequatio a making equal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 表平坦，aequare 表弄平，aequatio 表使相等。

items.example: The first vowel dropped in English.
items.exampleCN: 首音节元音在英语中脱落。

items.meaning: the act of pairing as equal

items.example: The noun precedes the verb historically.
A legal cousin on the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 同词干上的法律用语表亲。

items.example: The line that levels the globe.

definition_zh: 方程式；等式；复杂局面
definition_en: a mathematical statement that two things are equal, or a set of factors to balance
core_image: 等号两边放着同样多的东西，必须保持平衡
scene: 老师让学生在黑板上解一道简单的方程。The teacher asked a student to solve a simple equation on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 equation 是「方程式」（第 1 个义项：数学中用等号连接两边的式子）；句意：老师让学生在黑板上解一道简单的方程。

collocations.phrase: the other side of the equation

senses.title: A mathematical equation
senses.definition: a mathematical statement showing that two expressions are equal
senses.definitionCN: 表明两个表达式相等的数学陈述
senses.example: This equation has two possible answers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程有两个可能的解。
senses.why: The noun comes from a Latin verb meaning to make equal, so it names a statement of equality.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自意为「使相等」的拉丁动词，因此指一个表示相等的陈述。

senses.title: A chemical equation
senses.definition: a symbolic statement that balances the atoms on each side of a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 用符号表示反应两边原子数平衡的式子
senses.example: The class balanced the chemical equation together.
senses.exampleCN: 全班一起配平了这个化学方程式。
senses.why: Chemistry borrows the equal-sign form to show that matter is conserved.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用等号形式来表示物质守恒。

senses.title: A set of factors to balance
senses.titleCN: 复杂局面；需权衡的因素
senses.definition: a situation in which several factors must be weighed together
senses.definitionCN: 必须把多个因素放在一起权衡的情形
senses.example: Cost is only one part of the equation.
senses.exampleCN: 成本只是需要权衡的因素之一。
senses.why: If an equation balances two sides, a real situation can be pictured as sides to weigh.
senses.whyCN: 如果方程要平衡两边，现实局面也可以被想象成需要权衡的两边。

intro.en: Equation comes from Latin aequatio, a making equal, from aequare, to make level, and aequus, level.
intro.cn: equation 来自拉丁语 aequatio（使相等），源于 aequare（使平）与 aequus（平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、公平的。

items.en: Aequare means to make equal or level.
items.cn: aequare 意为使相等、使平。

items.en: Aequatio names the act of making equal.
items.cn: aequatio 指使相等的动作。

items.en: Équation applies the word to algebra.
items.cn: 法语 équation 把这个词用于代数。

items.en: Modern English extends equation to chemistry and to mixed situations.
items.cn: 现代英语把 equation 扩展到化学与复杂局面。

note.en: Equation is a balance word from the aequus family, close to formula and expression.
note.cn: equation 是来自 aequus 词族的「平衡」词，与 formula 和 expression 相邻。

entries.definition: to treat as equal
entries.definitionCN: 等同；使相等

entries.definition: relating to an equation
entries.definitionCN: 方程式的

entries.definition: the same in amount
entries.definitionCN: 相等的

entries.definition: a rule or relationship written in symbols
entries.definitionCN: 公式

entries.definition: a group of mathematical symbols
entries.definitionCN: 表达式

entries.definition: an equation true for all values
entries.definitionCN: 恒等式

normalIntro.en: Equation is a little balance: whatever is on one side of the equal sign must match the other.
normalIntro.cn: equation 是一架小天平：等号一边的东西必须与另一边相配。

normal.en: To solve an equation is to find the value that keeps both sides equal.
normal.cn: 解方程就是找出让两边保持相等的值。

normal.en: A linear equation draws a straight line on a graph.
normal.cn: 线性方程在图上画出一条直线。

normal.en: A chemical equation must be balanced atom by atom.
normal.cn: 化学方程式必须逐个原子配平。

normal.en: The other side of the equation means the factors you forgot.
normal.cn: 「the other side of the equation」指你忽略的另一面因素。

normal.en: Compare formula: a formula is a rule, an equation states equality.
normal.cn: 对比 formula：formula 是规则，equation 陈述相等关系。

abstract.en: Picture an equal sign holding two trays level.
abstract.cn: 想象一个等号托着两只水平的托盘。

abstract.en: Imagine atoms counted carefully on both sides of an arrow.
abstract.cn: 想象箭头两边被仔细数过的原子。

abstract.en: Think of a scale where cost sits on one pan and benefit on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一边是成本，一边是收益。

examples.en: She solved the equation in her head.
examples.cn: 她心算解出了这个方程。

examples.en: Every chemical equation must balance.
examples.cn: 每个化学方程式都必须配平。

examples.en: Time is the missing factor in the equation.
examples.cn: 时间是这一局面中缺失的因素。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equ + ation」——把两边「弄成一样」，就是方程式；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的）→ aequare（使相等）→ aequatio（使相等）→ 法语 équation → 英语 equation，核心义「两边相等的陈述」。

sensesIntro.en: Equation begins as a statement of mathematical equality, extends to chemistry, and then to any set of factors to balance.
sensesIntro.cn: equation 从数学上的相等陈述开始，扩展到化学，再扩展到任何需要权衡的因素组合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sides of an equal sign held in balance.
core.cn: 核心意象：等号两边保持平衡。

branches.en: The mathematical statement is the core sense.
branches.cn: 数学陈述是核心义项。

branches.en: Chemistry applies the equal-sign form to atoms.
branches.cn: 化学把等号形式用于原子。

branches.en: A real situation becomes sides that must be weighed.
branches.cn: 现实局面变成需要权衡的两边。

branches.en: Both a math equation and a hard choice involve balancing sides.
branches.cn: 数学方程与艰难选择都涉及平衡两边。

branches.en: Both math and chemistry equations must stay balanced.
branches.cn: 数学方程与化学方程式都必须保持平衡。

intro.en: Equation is a Latin noun of making equal, and English builds equate and equational around the same root.
intro.cn: equation 是拉丁语中表示「使相等」的名词，英语围绕同一词根构成 equate 与 equational。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level, aequare means to make equal, and aequatio means a making equal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的，aequare 意为使相等，aequatio 意为使相等的过程。

definition_zh: 赤道；赤道地区；天赤道；磁赤道；热赤道；（细胞的）赤道面
definition_en: the great circle around the earth halfway between the poles, or a corresponding line on another sphere
core_image: 一只橙子被横着切开，刀口绕行一圈，正好把球分成上下相等两半
scene: 课堂上老师拿一只橙子演示地球的横切大圆。A teacher draws a line around an orange to show where the equator would cut the globe.
sceneCN: 这里 equator 指「地球表面与南北两极等距的大圆」（第 1 个义项：把地球分成南北两半的零度纬线）；句意为老师用橙子演示这条大圆落在球面上的位置。图中可辨识物件：橙子、横切刀痕、地球仪、粉笔线。

derivatives.zh: 赤道的；赤道地区的 / 赤道仪

senses.title: The earth's great circle
senses.titleCN: 地球赤道：与两极等距的大圆
senses.definition: the great circle around the earth that lies halfway between the north and south poles and marks zero latitude
senses.definitionCN: 绕地球一圈、位于南北两极正中并标出零度纬线的大圆
senses.example: The river crosses the equator twice on its long course.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河在漫长的流程中两次越过赤道。
senses.why: Latin aequator meant 'equalizer'; the circle is named for making day and night equal, and it is the zero line from which latitude is counted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 aequator 意为「使相等者」；这条圈因使昼夜等长而得名，也是计算纬度的零度线。

senses.title: The equatorial region
senses.titleCN: 赤道地区：赤道两侧的湿热地带
senses.definition: the hot, humid belt of the earth near the equator
senses.definitionCN: 赤道附近炎热潮湿的地带
senses.example: Rubber plantations thrive in the equator's rain belt.
senses.exampleCN: 橡胶园在赤道雨带里生长旺盛。
senses.why: The line marks a climate as well as a coordinate, so the region around it is called the equator in ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 这条线既标坐标也标气候，因此它周围的地区在日常说法里也叫 the equator。

senses.title: The celestial equator
senses.titleCN: 天赤道：天球上与地球赤道对应的大圆
senses.definition: the great circle on the celestial sphere lying in the plane of the earth's equator
senses.definitionCN: 天球上位于地球赤道平面内的大圆
senses.example: The sun crosses the celestial equator at the equinoxes.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳在二分点时穿过天赤道。
senses.why: Astronomers projected the earth's equator onto the sky, where it serves as the zero line for declination.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家把地球赤道投影到天空，用作赤纬的零度线。

senses.title: The magnetic equator
senses.titleCN: 磁赤道：地磁场的零倾角线
senses.definition: the line around the earth where a magnetic needle stays horizontal and magnetic dip is zero
senses.definitionCN: 地球表面磁针保持水平、磁倾角为零的连线
senses.example: Compasses behave differently near the magnetic equator.
senses.exampleCN: 在磁赤道附近，指南针的表现不同。
senses.why: The magnetic field has its own symmetry plane, so it produces an 'equator' that does not match the geographic one.
senses.whyCN: 磁场有自己的对称面，因此产生一条与地理赤道不重合的「赤道」。

senses.title: The thermal equator
senses.titleCN: 热赤道：地表年均最高温的连线
senses.definition: the line of highest mean annual temperature, which shifts with the seasons and with land distribution
senses.definitionCN: 年平均气温最高的连线，随季节与海陆分布而移动
senses.example: The thermal equator lies north of the geographic equator in July.
senses.exampleCN: 七月时热赤道位于地理赤道以北。
senses.why: Heat, not geometry, defines this belt, yet its central line is still pictured as an equator.
senses.whyCN: 定义这条带的是热量而非几何，但它的中心线仍被想象成一条赤道。

senses.title: The cell equator
senses.titleCN: 细胞赤道：有丝分裂中期染色体排列的平面
senses.definition: the plane midway between the two poles of a dividing cell, where chromosomes line up
senses.definitionCN: 分裂细胞两极之间的中间平面，染色体在此排列
senses.example: Chromosomes align at the cell equator before separating.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体在分离前排列在细胞赤道面上。
senses.why: A dividing cell has two poles like a small sphere, so the plane halfway between them borrows the name equator.
senses.whyCN: 分裂的细胞像一个小球有两极，因此两极之间的平面借用了赤道之名。

senses.title: A great circle of any sphere
senses.titleCN: 任意球体的大圆：与自转轴垂直的等分圈
senses.definition: any great circle perpendicular to the axis of a sphere or spheroid
senses.definitionCN: 与球体或椭球体自转轴垂直的任一大圆
senses.example: Surveyors computed the equator of the model dome.
senses.exampleCN: 测量员计算了模型穹顶的赤道圈。
senses.why: The earth's equator is only one instance of a general geometric relation, which can be applied to any rounded body.
senses.whyCN: 地球赤道只是一般几何关系的一个实例，可套用到任何近球体。

senses.title: A dividing line between halves
senses.titleCN: 平分线：把事物分成相等两半的界线
senses.definition: a line imagined as dividing something into two equal parts
senses.definitionCN: 被想象为把某物分成相等两半的界线
senses.example: The negotiators drew an equator through the disputed budget.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判者把有争议的预算划出一条对半分的界线。
senses.why: The word's core image, a line that makes two sides equal, can be moved from geography to any divided whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心意象——一条使两边相等的线——可以从地理移到任何被分割的整体。

intro.en: Equator is from Medieval Latin aequator 'equalizer', from aequare 'to make equal', built on aequus 'level, equal'. The geographical name began as a phrase about the circle that equalizes day and night. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: equator 来自中世纪拉丁 aequator「使相等者」，源于 aequare「使相等」，其词根为 aequus「平的、相等的」；地理名称最初是一个关于「使昼夜相等之圈」的短语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aequus meant 'level, even, equal'. Its deeper origin is not settled; the connection sometimes suggested to a root meaning 'even' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: aequus 意为「平的、均匀的、相等的」；其更深来源没有定论，有时提出的与「平」有关的词根联系属重构形式。

items.en: Aequare meant 'to make level or equal', a verb formed from aequus.
items.cn: aequare 意为「使平、使相等」，是由 aequus 构成的动词。

items.en: Aequator, 'one who equalizes', was used for the circle that makes day and night equal.
items.cn: aequator 意为「使相等者」，被用来指使昼夜等长的那条圈。

items.en: The older phrase circulus aequator diei et noctis, 'the circle equalizing day and night', explains why the line received this name.
items.cn: 更早的短语 circulus aequator diei et noctis 意为「使昼夜相等之圈」，说明了这条线得名的原因。

items.en: English geography adopted equator for the zero-latitude circle in the seventeenth century, dropping the rest of the phrase.
items.cn: 英语地理学在 17 世纪采用 equator 指零度纬线圈，省去了短语的其余部分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first dates): the pre-Latin origin of aequus is unresolved, and the earliest English uses of the magnetic and thermal senses are not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：aequus 在拉丁语之前的来源尚无定论，磁赤道与热赤道在英语中的最早用法亦无确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin 'equal' stock; group two holds the geographic lines and belts it is paired with.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「相等」词干的词；第二组是常与赤道配对的地理线与地带。

entries.definition: From aequatio 'a making equal': a statement that two quantities are equal, with no geographical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 aequatio「使相等」：表示两个量相等的式子，不含地理意义。

entries.definition: Aequus 'equal' plus latus 'side': a figure whose sides are all equal.
entries.definitionCN: aequus「相等」加 latus「边」：各边相等的图形。

entries.definition: Aequus plus valere 'be worth': equal in value or effect, not equal in shape.
entries.definitionCN: aequus 加 valere「有价值」：价值或效果相等，而非形状相等。

entries.definition: Built on aequus directly: the same in amount, degree, or value.
entries.definitionCN: 直接建在 aequus 之上：数量、程度或价值相同。

entries.definition: The region between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, which contains the equator but is wider.
entries.definitionCN: 南北回归线之间的地带，包含赤道但范围更宽。

entries.definition: A circle parallel to the equator; the equator is the zero-degree parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 与赤道平行的圈；赤道就是零度纬线。

entries.definition: The angular distance from the equator, not the line itself.
entries.definitionCN: 相对赤道的角距离，不是那条线本身。

entries.definition: A great circle through the poles; meridians cross the equator at right angles.
entries.definitionCN: 过两极的大圆；经线与赤道正交。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin 'equalizer', real geographic lines and real cell biology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「使相等者」、真实的地理线与真实的细胞生物学，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Aequus 'equal' + -ator 'one who makes': the circle that makes day and night equal.
normal.cn: aequus「相等」+ -ator「使……者」：使昼夜相等的那条圈。

normal.en: The equator is the zero-degree parallel; latitude is counted up and down from it.
normal.cn: 赤道是零度纬线；纬度从它向南北计数。

normal.en: The celestial equator is the earth's equator projected onto the sky.
normal.cn: 天赤道是地球赤道投影到天空的结果。

normal.en: The magnetic equator is where a compass needle lies flat.
normal.cn: 磁赤道是磁针保持水平的地方。

normal.en: In cell division, chromosomes line up on the cell equator, also called the metaphase plate.
normal.cn: 细胞分裂时染色体排在细胞赤道上，也叫中期板。

abstract.en: Picture a belt worn exactly around the middle of a ball.
abstract.cn: 想象一条带子正好系在球的正中间。

abstract.en: Picture a knife cutting an orange into two equal cups.
abstract.cn: 想象一刀把橙子切成两只相等的杯状半。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn through a budget so that both sides get the same amount.
abstract.cn: 想象在预算中间划一条线，让两边得到相同的数额。

examples.en: The equator passes through several countries in Africa and South America.
examples.cn: 赤道穿过非洲和南美洲的若干国家。

examples.en: Temperatures stay high near the equator all year.
examples.cn: 赤道附近全年气温都很高。

examples.en: The celestial equator is the zero line for declination.
examples.cn: 天赤道是赤纬的零度线。

dict_mnemonic.text: equa（相等，如 equal）+ tor（……者）→ 使昼夜相等的线 → 赤道

root: 中世纪拉丁 aequator「使相等者」= aequare「使相等」（aequus「平的、相等的」）+ -ator；原指使昼夜相等之圈，后在英语中指零度纬线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all use one image, a line that divides a round body into two equal halves: the earth's zero latitude, its hot belt, the sky's projection, the magnetic and thermal lines, the cell's mid-plane, any sphere's great circle, and a figurative dividing line.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用一个意象：把圆体分成相等两半的线——地球的零度纬线、湿热地带、天空中的投影、磁与热的对应线、细胞的中间平面、任意球体的大圆，以及比喻性的平分线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a belt drawn around the middle of a sphere, making the two halves equal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条绕球体中部的带子，使两半相等。

branches.en: THE LINE: the earth's zero circle is one case of a general great circle perpendicular to an axis.
branches.cn: 这条线：地球的零度圈是与轴垂直的一般大圆的一个实例。

branches.en: THE BELT: climate turns a geometric line into a hot region, and heat draws its own central line.
branches.cn: 地带：气候把几何线变成炎热区域，热量又画出自己的中心线。

branches.en: THE SKY: the earth's equator is projected outward as the celestial equator.
branches.cn: 天空：地球赤道向外投影为天赤道。

branches.en: THE FIELD: magnetism produces a second equator that does not match the geographic one.
branches.cn: 场：磁性产生第二条与地理赤道不重合的赤道。

branches.en: DIVISION: a cell's mid-plane and a figurative halfway line both repeat the equal-halves gesture.
branches.cn: 分割：细胞的中间平面与比喻的对半线都重复了「等分」动作。

intro.en: Equator belongs to a Latin family built on aequus 'equal'; the same root yields equality, equation and adequate.
intro.cn: equator 属于以拉丁 aequus「相等」为根的词族；同一词根还衍生 equality、equation 与 adequate。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus 'level, equal' yields aequare 'to make equal', aequator 'equalizer' and aequatio 'equation'; English keeps the family in equal, equity and equator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aequus「平的、相等」衍生 aequare「使相等」、aequator「使相等者」与 aequatio「等式」；英语以 equal、equity 与 equator 保留这个词族。

items.example: The root names balance between two sides.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根表示两边之间的均衡。

items.example: The verb supplies the action of equalizing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「使相等」的动作。

items.example: The noun first named the circle that equalizes day and night.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初指使昼夜相等的圈。

items.example: The equator divides the globe into two halves.

items.exampleCN: 赤道的热量催生强风暴。

items.example: The law aims at equality before the courts.
items.exampleCN: 法律追求法庭面前的平等。

items.example: The equinox occurs twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 昼夜平分点每年出现两次。

items.example: The supply was adequate for the winter.

definition_zh: 平衡；均衡；（物理）平衡态；（经济）市场均衡；（情绪）平静
definition_en: a state in which opposing forces or influences are balanced, so nothing tends to change
core_image: 一架天平两端重量相等，指针停在中央刻度上
scene: 走钢丝的人在风中调整手里的长杆，让身体停在正中不再倾斜。The tightrope walker adjusted the pole until the body reached equilibrium above the wire.
sceneCN: 走钢丝的人在风中调整长杆，让身体停在正中不再倾斜；句中的 equilibrium 指「相反的力量相抵、系统不再偏移的状态」（第 1 个义项：物理意义上的受力平衡）。图中可辨识物件：钢丝、长杆、稳定姿态、远处的风旗。

pos.zh: 平衡；均衡；平静（复数 equilibria）
均衡的（作定语，如 equilibrium state）

senses.title: Balance of physical forces
senses.definition: the state in which the forces acting on a body cancel out
senses.definitionCN: 作用在一个物体上的力相互抵消的状态
senses.example: The tightrope walker adjusted the pole until the body reached equilibrium above the wire.
senses.exampleCN: 走钢丝的人调整长杆，直到身体在钢丝上方达到平衡。
senses.why: The Latin word joins 'level' and 'scales', so the first sense is simply a pair of pans that no longer tips.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词把「平」与「天平」合在一起，因此第一义就是一架不再倾斜的天平。

senses.title: Chemical balance of two reactions
senses.definition: the state in which a forward reaction and its reverse proceed at equal rates
senses.definitionCN: 正反应与逆反应速率相等的状态
senses.example: The mixture reaches equilibrium when both reactions run at the same rate.
senses.exampleCN: 当两个反应以相同速率进行时，混合物达到平衡。
senses.why: Two opposing processes cancelling is the same picture as two weights cancelling, applied to rates instead of forces.
senses.whyCN: 两个相反过程相互抵消，与两个重量相抵是同一幅图，只是把力换成了速率。

senses.title: Market balance of supply and demand
senses.definition: the price and quantity at which the amount offered equals the amount wanted
senses.definitionCN: 供给量与需求量相等时的价格与数量
senses.example: The market found equilibrium at a price neither side had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 市场在一个双方都没预料到的价位上达到均衡。
senses.why: Economics borrowed the word because a market that stops moving looks like a beam that has levelled.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用这个词，因为停止波动的市场就像一根已经放平的横梁。

senses.title: Emotional composure
senses.definition: a calm inner state in which opposing feelings do not pull a person about
senses.definitionCN: 相反情绪不再把人拉来拉去的平静内心状态
senses.example: Years of practice gave her an equilibrium that no insult could shake.
senses.exampleCN: 多年历练给了她一种任何侮辱都撼不动的平静。
senses.why: The metaphor moves inward: the opposing weights become feelings, and the level beam becomes a steady temper.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转向内心：相抵的重量变成情绪，水平的横梁变成稳定的性情。

senses.title: Biological and ecological balance
senses.definition: the steady internal or ecological state that a living system maintains
senses.definitionCN: 生命系统维持的内部或生态稳定状态
senses.example: Reef fish keep a rough equilibrium with the corals they feed on.
senses.exampleCN: 礁鱼与它们取食的珊瑚之间维持着大致平衡。
senses.why: A living system held steady by opposing processes is the same idea as a body held steady by opposing forces.
senses.whyCN: 生命系统靠相反过程维持稳定，与物体靠相反的力维持稳定是同一想法。

senses.title: A steady state with no tendency to change
senses.titleCN: 不再有变化趋势的稳定状态
senses.definition: a general condition in which nothing pushes the system away from where it is
senses.definitionCN: 没有任何因素把系统推离原位的总体状态
senses.example: After the shock, the system slowly returned to equilibrium.
senses.exampleCN: 冲击过后，系统慢慢回到平衡。
senses.why: Stripped of physics and markets, the core is simply rest, a state that no push disturbs.
senses.whyCN: 去掉物理与市场的具体内容，核心就是静止——一种没有推力能打扰的状态。

senses.title: A strategy nobody gains by changing
senses.titleCN: 无人因单独改变而获益的策略均衡
senses.definition: in game theory, a profile of choices in which no player gains by switching alone
senses.definitionCN: 博弈论中任何一方单独改变选择都无利可图的局面
senses.example: Neither firm could improve its payoff, so the pair settled into equilibrium.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司都无法提高收益，于是这一对选择进入均衡。
senses.why: The word is used for a balance of incentives rather than of forces, yet the shape is the same.
senses.whyCN: 这里平衡的是激励而非力，但形状仍然相同。

senses.title: Thermal equilibrium
senses.definition: the condition in which two bodies in contact exchange no net heat
senses.definitionCN: 两个接触物体之间没有净热量交换的状态
senses.example: The two blocks reached thermal equilibrium at the same temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 两块物体在同一温度下达到热平衡。
senses.why: Heat flow stops exactly when the two sides level off, which is the scales image made literal.
senses.whyCN: 热流恰在两侧齐平之时停止，这正是天平意象的字面版本。

intro.en: Equilibrium is Latin aequilibrium 'level balance', from aequus 'level, equal' and libra 'balance, scales'. English took it in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: equilibrium 来自拉丁 aequilibrium「水平的平衡」，由 aequus「平的、相等的」与 libra「天平」构成，十七世纪进入英语。

items.en: Aequus meant 'level, even, equal' and also 'calm, fair'. It gives equal, equity, equator and equable.
items.cn: aequus 意为「平的、齐的、相等的」，也表示「平静、公正」；它衍生 equal、equity、equator 与 equable。

items.en: Libra meant 'balance, scales' and also a unit of weight, roughly a pound; the zodiac sign took the same name.
items.cn: libra 意为「天平、秤」，也指一种重量单位，约合一磅；黄道十二宫的「天秤座」沿用此名。

items.en: Aequus plus libra produced aequilibrium, 'a level balance', used for physical balance and later for balance of mind.
items.cn: aequus 加 libra 构成 aequilibrium「水平的平衡」，先用于物理平衡，后也用于心境。

items.en: English adopted the word in the 1600s, at first for physical and mechanical balance.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪吸收这个词，最初用于物理与力学的平衡。

items.en: Nineteenth-century economics applied it to the price at which supply and demand meet, and the term became central to the discipline.
items.cn: 十九世纪经济学把它用于供需相遇的价格，这个词随后成为该学科的核心术语。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether English took the word directly from Latin or through French equilibre is not settled, and the earliest citation date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语是直接从拉丁语借入，还是经法语 equilibre 传入，尚无定论；最早书证年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin stock that are easily confused; group two holds near terms for balance.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词源、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示平衡的近义词。

entries.definition: Built on aequus alone: a steady, unvarying temper or climate, with no second element meaning balance.
entries.definitionCN: 只由 aequus 构成：指平稳不变的性情或气候，并没有表示「天平」的第二部分。

entries.definition: From aequus plus animus 'mind': calmness of mind, a cousin in meaning but not built on the scales image.
entries.definitionCN: 由 aequus 加 animus「心」构成：心平气和，意思相近，但并不建立在天平意象上。

entries.definition: From aequitas, 'evenness, fairness': justice or ownership value, not a physical balance.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 aequitas「均平、公正」：指公平或产权价值，不是物理平衡。

entries.definition: An English formation from equi- 'equal' and poise 'weight': a balanced state, close in meaning but not from the Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 英语自造词，由 equi-「相等」与 poise「重量」构成：平衡状态，意思接近但并非来自那个拉丁名词。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for an even distribution of weight or power; it is the everyday counterpart of equilibrium.
entries.definitionCN: 表示重量或力量均匀分布的日常词，是 equilibrium 的日常对应词。

entries.definition: The tendency to stay in place when pushed; equilibrium is the state, stability is how well it holds.
entries.definitionCN: 受推时保持原位的倾向；equilibrium 是状态，stability 是这种状态有多稳。

entries.definition: The specific biological term for a body holding its internal conditions steady; equilibrium is the wider word.
entries.definitionCN: 生物体维持内部条件稳定的专门术语；equilibrium 范围更广。

entries.definition: A state of standstill, often used of fluids or history; it names stillness rather than balanced forces.
entries.definitionCN: 停滞状态，常用于流体或历史；指静止而非力量相抵。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the fixed phrases and the real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、固定搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: Aequus 'level' plus libra 'scales': a pair of pans that stops tipping.
normal.cn: aequus「平」加 libra「天平」：一对不再倾斜的秤盘。

normal.en: The family runs equilibrium, equilibrate, equilibration, disequilibrium and nonequilibrium.
normal.cn: 同族词有 equilibrium、equilibrate、equilibration、disequilibrium 与 nonequilibrium。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: in equilibrium, thermal equilibrium, market equilibrium, stable equilibrium.
normal.cn: 固定说法：处于平衡、热平衡、市场均衡、稳定平衡。

normal.en: The same first element appears in equal, equity, equator and equable.
normal.cn: 同一前半出现在 equal、equity、equator 与 equable 中。

normal.en: Aequus also meant calm, which is why the word can describe a steady temper.
normal.cn: aequus 也含「平静」之意，所以这个词能形容稳定的性情。

abstract.en: Picture a beam that stops moving the moment its two pans carry the same weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一根横梁，两端负重相等的那一刻就停止摆动。

abstract.en: Picture a room where heat stops crossing the wall because both sides are equally warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，两侧一样暖时热量就不再穿墙。

abstract.en: Picture a mind pulled from both sides until the pull cancels and it simply stays.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗心被两侧拉扯，直到拉力相抵，它就原地不动。

examples.en: The reaction mixture took twenty minutes to reach equilibrium.
examples.cn: 反应混合物用了二十分钟达到平衡。

examples.en: Higher tariffs pushed the market away from its old equilibrium.
examples.cn: 更高的关税把市场推离了原来的均衡。

examples.en: She listened to the whole complaint with an unshaken equilibrium.
examples.cn: 她以毫不动摇的平静听完了整段抱怨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equi（相等）+ librium（天平）——两边相等，秤就平了」

root: 拉丁 aequilibrium「水平的平衡」= aequus「平的、相等的」+ libra「天平、秤」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image, a beam that levels: forces, reaction rates, market price, temper, living systems, plain rest, incentives and heat flow.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一幅图——一根放平的横梁：力、反应速率、市场价格、性情、生命系统、单纯的静止、激励与热流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scales whose pointer rests exactly at the middle mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架指针正停在中央刻度的天平。

branches.en: WEIGHT: mechanical forces and heat flow both stop when the two sides level.
branches.cn: 重量：力学上的力与热流，都在两侧齐平时停止。

branches.en: NATURAL PROCESSES: reaction rates match, and living systems hold their inner conditions steady.
branches.cn: 自然过程：反应速率相符，生命系统则维持内部条件稳定。

branches.en: SETTLED MARKET AND MERE REST: price stops moving, and any system stops being pushed.
branches.cn: 市场与静止：价格不再变动，任何系统也不再被推动。

branches.en: MIND: composure is a balance of feelings that nobody can see.
branches.cn: 内心：平静是一种看不见的情绪平衡。

branches.en: INCENTIVES: no player gains by moving alone, so the choices stay put.
branches.cn: 激励：无人因单独改变而获益，选择因此停在原处。

intro.en: Equilibrium is two Latin words welded together, and each half still builds English words on its own.
intro.cn: equilibrium 由两个拉丁词焊接而成，两半各自仍能构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus gives equal, equity, equator and equable; libra gives Libra and the sense of weighing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aequus 衍生 equal、equity、equator 与 equable；libra 衍生 Libra 及「称量」之义。

items.example: The first half of the word carries the idea of evenness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的前半带着「均平」的意思。

items.meaning: balance, scales; a unit of weight
items.example: The second half supplies the picture of weighing.

items.exampleCN: 两个腔室一夜之间达到平衡。

items.example: The shock caused a brief disequilibrium.
items.exampleCN: 冲击造成了短暂的失衡。
非平衡系统需要持续供能。

items.example: He kept an equable temper all day.
Pay equity was the central demand.

definition_zh: 装备；配备；使有能力
definition_en: to supply someone or something with the tools or skills needed
core_image: 出发前把工具一件件装进背包
scene: 学校为每间实验室配备了新的显微镜。The school equipped every lab with new microscopes.
sceneCN: 这里 equipped 是 equip 的过去式，表示「配备」（第 1 个义项：提供所需的工具或设备）；句意：学校为每间实验室配备了新的显微镜。

senses.title: To supply with tools or gear
senses.definition: to provide a person or place with the tools, machines, or gear needed
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某地提供所需的工具、机器或装备
senses.example: The team was equipped with maps and radios.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍配备了地图和无线电。
senses.why: The word came from fitting out a ship, so the basic sense is supplying the necessary gear.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指为船只配备物资，因此基本含义是提供必需的装备。

senses.title: To prepare someone with skills
senses.definition: to give someone the knowledge or skills needed for a task
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人完成任务所需的知识或技能
senses.example: The course equips students to work in hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程使学生有能力在医院工作。
senses.why: Equipment can be mental as well as physical, so the verb extends to training.
senses.whyCN: 装备既可以是物质的，也可以是头脑中的，所以动词扩展到培训。

senses.title: To fit out a place
senses.definition: to furnish a room, building, or vehicle with what it needs
senses.definitionCN: 为房间、建筑或车辆配置所需设备
senses.example: They equipped the new kitchen with modern appliances.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为新厨房配置了现代电器。
senses.why: The same supplying action applies to places and vehicles, not only to people.
senses.whyCN: 同样的供给动作也适用于场所和车辆，而不只是人。

intro.en: Equip comes from Old French esquiper, to fit out a ship, probably from a Germanic word for ship.
intro.cn: equip 来自古法语 esquiper（为船只配备物资），可能源于日耳曼语中表示「船」的词。

items.en: A Germanic skip word means ship.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中 skip 一词意为船。

items.en: Esquiper means to fit out a ship.
items.cn: esquiper 意为为船只配备物资。

items.en: The word extends to fitting out a person or army.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到为个人或军队配备。

items.en: Equip enters English with the gear sense.
items.cn: equip 以「装备」的含义进入英语。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of preparing with skills.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「以技能作准备」的含义。

note.en: Equip is a supplying verb, closely tied to equipment and to words for furnishing.
note.cn: equip 是表示供给的动词，与 equipment 以及表示配置的词关系紧密。

abstract.cn: 想象水手把绳索和灯笼装上船。

abstract.en: Imagine a hiker checking each item in a backpack.
abstract.cn: 想象徒步者逐一检查背包里的物品。

abstract.en: Think of a student leaving a class with a new skill.
abstract.cn: 想象一名学生带着新技能走出课堂。

examples.en: Rescue teams were equipped with warm clothing.
examples.cn: 救援队配备了保暖衣物。

examples.en: The training equips nurses to handle emergencies.

examples.en: They equipped the office with new computers.
examples.cn: 他们为办公室配备了新电脑。

definition_zh: 设备；装备；器材
definition_en: the tools, machines, or gear needed for a particular purpose
core_image: 一堆工具整齐摆开，随时可以带上出发
scene: 登山前，队员检查了所有装备。Before the climb, the team checked all their equipment.
sceneCN: 这里 equipment 是「装备」（第 1 个义项：为特定目的所需的工具和器材）；句意：登山前，队员检查了所有装备。

senses.title: Tools and machines for a purpose
senses.definition: the set of tools or machines used for a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于某项活动的整套工具或机器
senses.example: The lab bought new equipment for the students.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室为学生购买了新设备。
senses.why: The noun adds -ment to equip, naming all the things supplied rather than the act of supplying.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 equip 加 -ment 构成，指被配备的全部物品，而不是配备的动作。

senses.title: Special gear for an activity
senses.definition: the clothing or gear needed for a sport, job, or journey
senses.definitionCN: 运动、工作或旅行所需的服装或装备
senses.example: Climbing equipment must be checked before every trip.
senses.exampleCN: 每次出行前都必须检查登山装备。
senses.why: Equipment can be personal gear as well as shared machines.
senses.whyCN: equipment 既可以是共用机器，也可以是个人装备。

senses.title: The act of fitting out
senses.definition: the process of supplying a person or place with what is needed, used in formal contexts
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某地提供所需之物的过程，用于正式语境
senses.example: The equipment of the new hospital took a full year.
senses.exampleCN: 新医院的设备配置花了整整一年。
senses.why: The suffix -ment can name an action as well as its result, which keeps the older process sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ment 既可指动作也可指结果，因此保留了较老的「过程」含义。
