definition_zh: 公平；公正；股权；权益；资产净值；衡平法
definition_en: fairness in the way people are treated, or the value of an owner's share in an asset
core_image: 水灾过后，富户能搬进旅馆，穷人只能住体育馆，市议会按实际损失发放补助，努力把起点上的差距补平
scene: 洪水过后议事会分发救济。The council distributed relief with an eye to equity rather than equal shares.
sceneCN: 此处指「按实际需要与损失分配、以求结果公平」（第 1 个义项：公正对待，而非机械平均）；句意为水灾之后，议会发放救济时看重的是公平，而非每人一份的平均分配。可辨识物件：临时旅馆、体育馆床位、补助登记表、泥水痕迹。

senses.title: Fairness in treatment
senses.definition: the quality of treating people justly, especially by adjusting for differences in need or disadvantage
senses.definitionCN: 公正待人的品质，尤指按需要或不利处境作出调整
senses.example: After the flood, the council distributed relief with an eye to equity rather than equal shares.
senses.exampleCN: 水灾之后，议会发放救济时看重的是公平，而非每人一份的平均分配。
senses.why: Equity comes from Latin aequitas 'evenness, fairness', from aequus 'level, even', so the base sense is a level scale rather than an identical portion.
senses.whyCN: equity 来自拉丁 aequitas「均平、公正」，词根 aequus「平的、相等的」，因此基础义是「把秤放平」，而非「每份一样」。

senses.title: An ownership stake
senses.definition: a share of ownership in a company or asset, giving a claim on its value
senses.definitionCN: 在公司或资产中的一份所有权，可对其价值提出主张
senses.example: The founders kept a small equity stake after the second round of funding.
senses.exampleCN: 第二轮融资后，创始人仍保留一小部分股权。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the word because a fair share of value is literally a share in the asset, so 'fairness' became 'ownership portion'.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用这个词，因为价值中「应得的一份」字面上就是资产中的一份，于是「公平」转为「所有权份额」。

senses.title: Net value of an asset
senses.definition: the value of an asset after all claims against it are subtracted, as in home equity
senses.definitionCN: 扣除全部相关债务后资产的剩余价值，如房屋净值
senses.example: Their equity in the house grew as the mortgage was paid down.
senses.exampleCN: 随着房贷逐步偿还，他们在这栋房子上的净值增加了。
senses.why: The accounting sense measures what is truly the owner's, which is the ownership sense reduced to a number.
senses.whyCN: 会计义衡量真正属于所有者的部分，也就是把所有权义化成一个数字。

senses.title: The law of equity
senses.definition: the body of English law developed to soften the strictness of common law and to provide fair remedies
senses.definitionCN: 为缓和普通法的严苛并提供公平救济而形成的英国法律体系
senses.example: The court of equity granted an injunction where the common law could only award damages.
senses.exampleCN: 衡平法院签发了禁令，而普通法只能判决损害赔偿。
senses.why: Legal history used the word for fairness itself, and the name stuck to the court that administered it.
senses.whyCN: 法律史直接用「公平」一词来称呼这套制度，名称便固定在执行它的法院上。

senses.title: Equal treatment policy
senses.definition: a policy that aims to remove barriers so that groups can reach the same opportunities
senses.definitionCN: 旨在消除障碍、使不同群体获得相同机会的政策
senses.example: The university adopted an equity plan for students from the hill villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学为来自山村的学生制定了公平计划。
senses.why: Modern policy uses equity for the active removal of barriers, as distinct from formal equality of rules.
senses.whyCN: 现代政策用 equity 指主动消除障碍，与规则上的形式平等相区别。

senses.title: Residual claim in finance
senses.definition: the right of shareholders to what remains after all debts and other claims are paid
senses.definitionCN: 在清偿全部债务与其他主张后，股东对剩余部分的权利
senses.example: Equity holders are paid last, so they carry the greatest risk.
senses.exampleCN: 权益持有人最后受偿，因此承担最大风险。
senses.why: Because owners are paid last, the finance sense also names the riskiest claim, not just the largest one.
senses.whyCN: 由于所有者最后受偿，金融义也指风险最大的主张，而不只是最大的一份。

senses.title: Justice in distribution
senses.definition: the fairness of how goods, burdens and opportunities are distributed across a society
senses.definitionCN: 商品、负担与机会在一个社会中如何分配的公平性
senses.example: The report asked whether the tax system produced equity across the income scale.
senses.exampleCN: 报告追问税制是否在收入阶梯上实现了公平。
senses.why: Political philosophy widened the word from individual fairness to the fairness of a whole distribution.
senses.whyCN: 政治哲学把这个词从个人公平扩展到整个分配的公平。

senses.title: Equitable access in education
senses.definition: the principle that a person's background should not decide their access to schooling or support
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的出身不应决定其受教育或获得支持的机会这一原则
senses.example: Equity in admissions meant offering tutoring before the entrance test, not lowering the standard.
senses.exampleCN: 录取公平意味着在入学考试前提供辅导，而不是降低标准。
senses.why: Schools use the term for support given earlier, because fairness in access is judged by outcomes, not by identical treatment.
senses.whyCN: 学校用这个词指提前给予的支持，因为入学公平由结果衡量，而非由相同对待衡量。

intro.en: Equity comes from Latin aequitas 'evenness, fairness', from aequus 'level, even', through Old French. Its legal and financial senses grew in English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: equity 经古法语来自拉丁 aequitas「均平、公正」，词根 aequus「平的、相等的」。其法律与金融义在英语中发展出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aequus meant 'level, even, equal'. Its deeper origin is not established, and earlier forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: aequus 意为「平的、均等的、相等的」。其更深来源未得到证明，凡为其提出的更早形态均属重构。

items.en: Aequitas named evenness and fairness, the quality of a level scale. It was also personified as a Roman virtue.
items.cn: aequitas 指均平与公正，即秤杆放平的性质，也曾被拟人化为罗马美德。

items.en: Old French equite carried the word into English, where it first meant fairness of judgment.
items.cn: 古法语 equite 把这个词带入英语，最初指判断的公正。

items.en: English law developed courts of equity to give remedies that the strict common law could not, and the word became the name of that system.
items.cn: 英国法发展出衡平法院，以提供严格普通法无法给出的救济，这个词便成为该体系的名称。

items.en: From the seventeenth century equity also named the owner's share in a venture, since a fair portion of value is a portion of ownership.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，equity 也指所有者在事业中的份额，因为价值中应得的一份就是所有权的一份。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin origin of aequus is unsettled, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a documented word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：aequus 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形态均属重构，而非有书证的词。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same level root; group two holds terms about fairness or ownership that answer a different question.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「均平」词根的词；第二组是关于公平或所有权的说法，回答的是不同问题。

entries.definition: Means identical shares or status; equity asks for fair shares, which may differ.
entries.definitionCN: 指份额或地位相同；equity 要求公平份额，份额可以不同。

entries.definition: Means fair or just; it describes a decision or arrangement, not a financial stake.
entries.definitionCN: 意为公平的、公正的，描述决定或安排，不指金融份额。

entries.definition: Unfairness or unjust difference; it is the opposite of the fairness sense, not of the financial one.
entries.definitionCN: 指不公平或不公正差异，是公平义的反面，而非金融义的反面。

entries.definition: Calmness of mind, from aequus plus animus 'mind'; it shares the root but has nothing to do with fairness.
entries.definitionCN: 指心境的平静，由 aequus 加 animus「心」构成；同根但与公平无关。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for just treatment; equity is its formal and legal counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指公正对待的日常名词；equity 是其正式与法律对应语。

entries.definition: A broader ideal of right order and law; equity often names a corrective within that order.
entries.definitionCN: 指正当秩序与法律的更宽理想；equity 常指该秩序内的矫正。

entries.definition: The fact or right of possessing something; equity in finance is a measured share of that right.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有某物的事实或权利；金融中的 equity 是这一权利的可计量份额。

entries.definition: An interest or share in an enterprise; it is close to the financial sense but less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 指在事业中的利益或份额，接近金融义但较不技术化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin aequus 'level' gives equity: first a level scale, then a fair share, then an ownership share.
normal.cn: 拉丁 aequus「平的」给出 equity：先指放平的秤，再指公平的一份，再指所有权份额。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: pay equity, equity stake, home equity, court of equity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：薪酬公平、股权、房屋净值、衡平法院。

normal.en: The family runs equitable, equitably, inequity, inequitable, equal and equality.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 equitable、equitably、inequity、inequitable、equal 与 equality。

normal.en: The same root appears in equator, equilibrium and equanimity, all built on the idea of level.
normal.cn: 同一词根见于 equator、equilibrium 与 equanimity，都建立在「平」的观念上。

normal.en: Finance pays equity last, which is why the word also carries risk.
normal.cn: 金融中权益最后受偿，因此这个词也带着风险。

abstract.en: Picture a scale adjusted so that the lighter side is not simply outvoted.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤被调整过，较轻的一边不会因分量小而直接被压过去。

abstract.en: Picture a deed that names who truly owns the house after every loan is counted.
abstract.cn: 想象一张契据，数清每笔贷款后写明谁真正拥有这栋房子。

abstract.en: Picture a court that can order someone to stop, not merely to pay.
abstract.cn: 想象一个法院能命令某人停手，而不只是让其赔钱。

examples.en: The scholarship fund was designed for equity, not for equal awards to every applicant.
examples.cn: 这项奖学金着眼于公平，而非给每位申请者相同金额。

examples.en: She sold half her equity in the startup to pay for the factory.
examples.cn: 她卖掉初创公司一半股权，用来支付工厂费用。

examples.en: The ruling came from a court of equity and stopped the eviction.
examples.cn: 这项裁决出自衡平法院，阻止了驱逐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equal（相等）+ ity（性质）」——把秤放平 → 公平；自己应得的那一份 → 权益

root: equity 经古法语来自拉丁 aequitas「均平、公正」，词根 aequus「平的、相等的」；aequus 更深来源不确定，凡更早形态均属重构。同根词包括 equal、equality、equator、equilibrium。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one level scale: fair treatment, an ownership share, net value, the law of fairness, equal-access policy, the residual financial claim, distributive justice and fair access to schooling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一杆秤展开：公平对待、所有权份额、净值、衡平法、平权政策、剩余索取权、分配正义与教育机会公平。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale adjusted so that the lighter side is heard, not simply outweighed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杆被调整过的秤，较轻的一边也能被听见，而不只是被压过去。

branches.en: FAIR SCALE: fairness of treatment and fairness of distribution are the same level scale writ large.
branches.cn: 公平的秤：对待公平与分配公平，是同一杆秤放大后的样子。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP: a fair share becomes a stake, and the last-paid claim carries the risk.
branches.cn: 所有权：公平的一份变成股份，最后受偿的主张承担风险。

branches.en: NET VALUE: accounting reduces the stake to the number left after debts.
branches.cn: 净值：会计把股份化约为清偿债务后剩下的数字。

branches.en: LEGAL REMEDY: the court of fairness can order a stop, not merely a payment.
branches.cn: 法律救济：公平法院能命令停手，而不只是判赔。

branches.en: ACCESS: policy removes barriers before the test rather than lowering the standard after it.
branches.cn: 机会：政策在考试前消除障碍，而非在考试后降低标准。

intro.en: The noun comes from the Latin word for evenness, and its derived adjectives and negatives keep the same root.
intro.cn: 这个名词来自拉丁语表示「均平」的词，其派生形容词与反义词延续同一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus and aequitas supply the root; English built equitable, equitably, inequity and equality on the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aequus 与 aequitas 提供词根；英语在同一来源上造出 equitable、equitably、inequity 与 equality。

items.example: The root supplies the image of a level scale.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供水平秤的意象。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词变成名词。

items.example: The report found inequity in pay.

items.meaning: the level line around the earth

definition_zh: 相等的；等同的；对应物
definition_en: equal in value, meaning, or effect, or something that matches another
core_image: 两枚不同的硬币放在天平上，重量正好相同
scene: 一英里大约相当于一点六公里。One mile is roughly equivalent to one point six kilometers.
sceneCN: 这里 equivalent 是「相等的」（第 1 个义项：在价值、数量或意义上相同）；句意：一英里大约等于一点六公里。

senses.title: Equal in value or amount
senses.definition: having the same value, amount, or meaning as something else
senses.definitionCN: 在价值、数量或意义上与他人或他物相同
senses.example: A dollar is not equivalent to a euro.
senses.exampleCN: 一美元并不等于一欧元。
senses.why: Latin aequus means equal and valere means be worth, so equivalent literally means worth the same.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aequus 意为相等，valere 意为值，因此 equivalent 字面意思就是「价值相同」。

senses.title: Equal in effect or role
senses.definition: having the same result, function, or force as something else
senses.definitionCN: 产生相同结果、功能或效力的
senses.example: Silence was equivalent to agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默等同于同意。
senses.why: If two things are worth the same, they can stand in for each other in effect.
senses.whyCN: 如果两物价值相同，它们在效果上就可以互相替代。

senses.title: A matching thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that has the same value or role as another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或物具有相同价值或角色的人或物
senses.example: This word has no exact equivalent in English.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词在英语中没有完全对应的说法。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the matching item itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，指与之匹配的事物本身。

intro.en: Equivalent joins Latin aequus, equal, and valere, to be worth, so it means having equal worth.
intro.cn: equivalent 结合拉丁语 aequus（相等的）与 valere（值），意为具有相同的价值。

items.en: Aequus means equal or level.
items.cn: aequus 意为相等的、平的。

items.en: Valere means to be worth or be strong.
items.cn: valere 意为值、有力量。

items.en: Aequivalere means to be worth the same.
items.cn: aequivalere 意为价值相等。

items.en: Aequivalentem is the present participle form.
items.cn: aequivalentem 是现在分词形式。

items.en: Équivalent carries the word into French.
items.cn: équivalent 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Modern English uses equivalent as both adjective and noun.
items.cn: 现代英语中 equivalent 兼作形容词与名词。

note.en: Equivalent is a worth-matching word, close to its family and to words for comparability.
note.cn: equivalent 是表示「价值相配」的词，与自身词族以及表示可比性的词相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being equal in value
entries.definitionCN: 相等；等价

entries.definition: in an equivalent way
entries.definitionCN: 等价地

entries.definition: open to more than one meaning
entries.definitionCN: 含糊的；模棱两可的

entries.definition: similar enough to be compared
entries.definitionCN: 可比较的；类似的

entries.definition: equivalent in effect
entries.definitionCN: 等同于的

entries.definition: a person or thing matching another
entries.definitionCN: 对应的人或物

normalIntro.en: Equivalent is equal plus worth: two unlike things can still balance.
normalIntro.cn: equivalent 是「相等」加「价值」：两个不同的东西也可以彼此平衡。

normal.en: Equivalent to means equal in value or effect.
normal.cn: equivalent to 表示在价值或效果上等于。

normal.en: A silent answer can be equivalent to a yes.
normal.cn: 沉默的回答可能等同于同意。

normal.en: The noun equivalence names the equal state.
normal.cn: 名词 equivalence 指相等的状态。

normal.en: No exact equivalent means there is no perfect match.
normal.cn: no exact equivalent 表示没有完全对应的说法。

normal.en: Compare tantamount: tantamount is mostly about effect, equivalent is broader.
normal.cn: 对比 tantamount：tantamount 多指效果，equivalent 范围更广。

abstract.en: Picture two different coins balancing on a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚不同的硬币在天平上保持平衡。

abstract.en: Imagine a translator finding a matching phrase.
abstract.cn: 想象译者找到一个对应的说法。

abstract.en: Think of two roads that lead to the same town.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路通向同一座城镇。

examples.en: Ten dimes are equivalent to one dollar.
examples.cn: 十枚十分硬币等于一美元。

examples.en: For him, losing the match was equivalent to failure.
examples.cn: 对他来说，输掉比赛等同于失败。

examples.en: The Italian word has no equivalent in my language.
examples.cn: 这个意大利语词在我的语言里没有对应词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equi + valent」——两边「价值相等」，就是等值；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（相等的）＋ valere（值）→ aequivalere（价值相等）→ 法语 équivalent → 英语 equivalent，核心义「价值或作用相等」。

sensesIntro.en: Equivalent begins with equal value, extends to equal effect, and then names the matching thing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: equivalent 从价值相等开始，扩展到效果相同，再指与之匹配的事物本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two different coins balancing on one scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚不同的硬币在天平上平衡。

branches.en: Equal value is the literal core sense.
branches.cn: 价值相等是字面核心义项。

branches.en: Equal effect extends worth to results.
branches.cn: 效果相同把价值扩展到结果。

branches.en: The matching thing is the noun use.
branches.cn: 匹配之物是名词用法。

branches.en: Things of equal value often have equal effect.
branches.cn: 价值相等的事物往往效果也相同。

branches.en: A counterpart is the thing that carries equal value.
branches.cn: 对应物就是承载同等价值的事物。

intro.en: Equivalent combines a Latin equal root with a Latin worth root, plus English noun and adverb endings.
intro.cn: equivalent 结合拉丁语「相等」词根与「价值」词根，并加上英语名词和副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means equal and valere means to be worth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为相等，valere 意为值。

items.exampleCN: equivalent 保留结合后的含义。

definition_zh: 含糊其辞；支吾搪塞；两面讨好地说
definition_en: to use words that could mean two different things, deliberately avoiding a clear answer
core_image: 证席上一句话被劈成两半，左半承认右半否认，听者各自带走了想要的那一半
scene: 面对质问，部长一直含糊其辞。The minister equivocated under questioning.
sceneCN: 这里 equivocate 是「含糊其辞」（第 1 个义项：有意让话可以两解）；句意：部长在追问下一味支吾。

pos.zh: 含糊其辞；支吾搪塞；两面讨好地说

collocations.zh: 在记录上口头上模棱两可

senses.title: To speak so a phrase carries two senses
senses.titleCN: 含糊其辞；模棱两可地说
senses.definition: to phrase a reply so that two interpretations remain open, usually on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把回答说得保留两种解释，通常是有意为之
senses.example: Witnesses equivocated for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 证人们含糊其辞了好几个小时。
senses.why: The Latin source names an equal voice, one that calls in two directions at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁源头说的是「声音相等」，即同时朝两个方向招呼。

senses.title: To deny in order to escape
senses.definition: to deny or hedge in order to avoid responsibility or a direct answer
senses.definitionCN: 为推卸责任或回避直答而否认或打折扣
senses.example: He equivocated about the money.
senses.exampleCN: 关于那笔钱他闪烁其词。
senses.why: Casuistry gave the word its moral edge, since evasion wore the mask of careful speech.
senses.whyCN: 决疑论给了它道德锋芒，因为回避常披上谨慎言辞的外衣。

senses.title: To use a term with two meanings in argument
senses.definition: a technical use in logic, switching between senses of one word inside a proof
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学专门用法，在同一论证中切换一个词的不同义
senses.example: The syllogism equivocated on law.
senses.exampleCN: 这段三段论在「规律」一词上偷换了概念。
senses.why: Textbooks of logic keep the fallacy named after the verb.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学教本保留了以该动词命名的谬误。

intro.en: Equivocate is built on late Latin aequivocare, from aequus equal plus vocare to call.
intro.cn: equivocate 建在晚期拉丁语 aequivocare 之上，由 aequus「相等」加 vocare「呼唤」构成。

items.en: Vocare means to call.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼唤。

items.en: Aequus means equal or level.
items.cn: aequus 意为相等、平坦。

items.en: Aequivocare means to call equally, so to share one name.
items.cn: aequivocare 意为同等地呼名，因而共有一名。

items.en: aequivocatio names terms with several senses.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 aequivocatio 指多义之名。

items.en: English takes the verb with a moral shading.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语摄入该动词并带道德色彩。

items.en: Religious controversy makes evasion its central sense.
items.cn: 十七世纪宗教论争把回避推为核心义。

note.en: Group one holds the vocare calling family; group two holds other verbs of evasive speech.
note.cn: 第一组是 vocare 这一表呼唤的词族；第二组是其他表回避性言辞的动词。

entries.definition: Open to two readings, describing a reply rather than a speaker.
entries.definitionCN: 可作两读，形容回答而非说话人。

entries.definition: Of the voice, from vocare.
entries.definitionCN: 与声音有关，出自 vocare。

entries.definition: To call on a name for help or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 呼名以求助或引权威。

entries.definition: To make equal, sharing the level prefix of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 使相等，与本词共享表平的词头。

entries.definition: To speak falsely so as to mislead, more formal than equivocate.
entries.definitionCN: 说假话以误导，比 equivocate 更书面。

entries.definition: To qualify a statement so it cannot be pinned down.
entries.definitionCN: 为陈述加限制使其无法被钉住。

entries.definition: To avoid committing in order to buy time.
entries.definitionCN: 不表态以拖延时间。

entries.definition: To make language dark on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 故意把话说得晦涩。

normalIntro.en: Equivocal describes the words; equivocate describes the speaker doing it.
normalIntro.cn: equivocal 形容话语，equivocate 说说话的人。

normal.en: Follow with about, on, or over, not with a that-clause.
normal.cn: 后接 about、on 或 over，不接 that 从句。

normal.en: Journalists use it when a refusal is dressed as an answer.
normal.cn: 当拒绝被包装成回答时，记者用这个词。

normal.en: The noun equivocation is more common in law reports.
normal.cn: 法律报道中更常用名词 equivocation。

normal.en: In logic it names a fallacy, not dishonesty.
normal.cn: 在逻辑学中它命名一种谬误而非不诚实。

normal.en: Keep stress on the second syllable of the first foot.
normal.cn: 重音落在第一个音步的第二音节上。

abstract.en: Picture an umpire who says both players could be right.
abstract.cn: 想象一位说两名球员都不错的裁判。

abstract.en: Imagine a sentence with a door on each end.
abstract.cn: 想象一句两端各开一门的句子。

abstract.en: Think of a witness who answers questions with weather reports.
abstract.cn: 想想那位用谈天气来回应提问的证人。

examples.en: The minister equivocated until the chair cut him off.
examples.cn: 部长一味含糊其辞，直到主席打断他。

examples.en: Equivocating about dates helped no one in the inquiry.
examples.cn: 在日期上支吾搪塞对调查毫无助益。

examples.en: One equivocated term can sink a whole proof.
examples.cn: 一个两可的概念就能拖垮整个证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一鬼滑腔」——话里带鬼、腔调打滑，所以 equivocate 是含糊其辞、支吾搪塞；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（相等）＋ vocare（呼唤）→ aequivocare（同名异实）→ 晚期拉丁 aequivocatio（多义）→ 英语 equivocate，核心义「一个名字朝两个方向呼唤」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb covers deliberate ambiguity, evasive denial, and a named fallacy in logic.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词涵盖存意的两可、回避式的否认，以及逻辑学中命名的一种谬误。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one name called out so it lands on two different things.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个名字被喊出，同时落在两样不同的东西上。

branches.en: The speaker leaves both readings alive.
branches.cn: 说话人让两种解释都活着。

branches.en: Purpose turns ambiguity into escape.
branches.cn: 意图把两可变成脱身。

branches.en: Logic records the same move as a defect.
branches.cn: 逻辑学把同一手法记为缺陷。

branches.en: Both turn on a word with two senses.
branches.cn: 两者都系于一个多义之词。

branches.en: Both belong to speech under pressure.
branches.cn: 两者都属于压力之下的言说。

intro.en: A stem of levelness joins a stem of calling, and a frequentative ending makes the verb.
intro.cn: 表平等的词干接上表呼唤的词干，再以动频词尾构成动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare is to call, vocare nomen is to name, and aequare is to make equal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare 表呼唤，vocare nomen 表命名，aequare 表使相等。

items.example: A plain cousin on the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干上朴素的表亲词。

latinEntries.meaning: to call by the same name

definition_zh: 时代；纪元；地质年代
definition_en: a long period of history with a particular character
core_image: 一条长河被刻上标记，分成一段段可命名的时期
scene: 铁路的修建开启了这个地区的新时代。The railway opened a new era for the region.
sceneCN: 这里 era 是「时代」（第 1 个义项：具有某种特征的一段长时期）；句意：铁路的修建为这个地区开启了新时代。

senses.title: A period of history
senses.definition: a long period of history marked by particular events, ideas, or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 以特定事件、思想或状况为标志的一段长历史时期
senses.example: The invention of printing began a new era.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷术的发明开启了一个新时代。
senses.why: The word first meant a system of counting years, so it naturally names a marked stretch of history.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指纪年的体系，因此自然指一段被标记的历史时期。

senses.title: A notable period in a life
senses.definition: a period in a person's life associated with a particular activity or mood
senses.definitionCN: 与某种活动或情绪相关的一段个人生活时期
senses.example: Her teaching era lasted twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她的教学生涯持续了二十年。
senses.why: A historical era and a personal era are both bounded periods with a character.
senses.whyCN: 历史时代与个人时期都是具有某种特征的有界时期。

senses.title: A geological era
senses.definition: a major division of geological time, longer than a period
senses.definitionCN: 地质时间的主要划分，比「纪」更长
senses.example: Dinosaurs lived in the Mesozoic era.
senses.exampleCN: 恐龙生活在中生代。
senses.why: Geology borrows the general word for a very long, clearly divided span of time.
senses.whyCN: 地质学借用这个一般词，指极长且有明确划分的时间跨度。

intro.en: Era comes from Late Latin aera, a system of counting years, probably from Latin aes, bronze or money, whose plural is aera.
intro.cn: era 来自晚期拉丁语 aera（纪年体系），可能源于拉丁语 aes（青铜、钱币），其复数为 aera。

items.en: Aes means bronze or money.
items.cn: aes 意为青铜或钱币。

items.en: Aera is the plural of aes.
items.cn: aera 是 aes 的复数。

items.en: Aera means a system of counting years.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 aera 指纪年体系。

items.en: Era carries the dating sense into Romance languages.
items.cn: era 把纪年含义带入罗曼语。

items.en: Modern English broadens era to any notable period.
items.cn: 现代英语把 era 扩展到任何显著时期。

note.en: Era is a period word, with look-alike forms and near words for long spans of time.
note.cn: era 是表示「时期」的词，拥有形近形式以及与长时间跨度相邻的近义词。

entries.definition: the Latin plural of aes
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语 aes 的复数

entries.definition: more than one era
entries.definitionCN: 多个时代

entries.definition: to expose to air
entries.definitionCN: 使通气

entries.definition: a long period of history
entries.definitionCN: 时代；时期

entries.definition: a period marked by a major change
entries.definitionCN: 纪元；划时代时期

entries.definition: a length of time
entries.definitionCN: 时期；阶段

normalIntro.en: Era is a marked stretch of time: historians draw a line and give the years a name.
normalIntro.cn: era 是一段被标记的时间：历史学家画一条线，再给这些年岁一个名字。

normal.en: A new era begins when something important changes.
normal.cn: 当重要的事物发生变化，新时代就开始了。

normal.en: The digital era is the age of computers and networks.
normal.cn: digital era 是计算机与网络的时代。

normal.en: The plural eras covers several named periods.
normal.cn: 复数 eras 指多个被命名的时期。

normal.en: A geologic era is longer than a period.
normal.cn: 地质年代比「纪」更长。

normal.en: Compare epoch: an epoch is shorter and marked by a sharp change.
normal.cn: 对比 epoch：epoch 更短，以剧烈变化为标志。

abstract.en: Picture a long river with stones marking each stretch.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长河，用石头标出每一段。

abstract.en: Imagine a calendar page turning into a bright new color.
abstract.cn: 想象日历翻到崭新明亮的一页。

abstract.en: Think of layers of rock holding the bones of ancient animals.
abstract.cn: 想象岩层中藏着古代动物的骨骼。

examples.en: The internet changed the era of communication.
examples.cn: 互联网改变了通信的时代。

examples.en: Her acting era ended when she moved abroad.
examples.cn: 她移居国外后，演艺时期结束了。

examples.en: The Mesozoic era is famous for its dinosaurs.
examples.cn: 中生代以恐龙闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「era」——像日历上画出的一个「段」，就是时代；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aes（青铜、钱币，复数 aera）→ 晚期拉丁语 aera（纪年体系）→ 英语 era，核心义「被标记的一段长时间」。

sensesIntro.en: Era moves from a dating system to a historical age, then to a personal period, and finally to a geological division.
sensesIntro.cn: era 从纪年体系转为历史时代，再指个人时期，最后指地质年代。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long timeline cut into named stretches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长时间线被切成有名称的段落。

branches.en: A historical period is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 历史时期是现代主要义项。

branches.en: A personal period applies the same span to one life.
branches.cn: 个人时期把同样的跨度用于一生。

branches.en: A geological era is the longest technical use.
branches.cn: 地质年代是最长的技术用法。

branches.en: A person can define an era and also have an era of their own.
branches.cn: 一个人可以定义一个时代，也可以拥有自己的时期。

branches.en: Both history and geology divide time into named eras.
branches.cn: 历史学与地质学都把时间划分为有名称的时代。

intro.en: Era is a short Latin-derived noun whose English family grows mainly through compounds.
intro.cn: era 是源自拉丁语的短名词，其英语词族主要通过复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin aes means bronze or money, and its plural aera leads to the dating sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aes 意为青铜或钱币，其复数 aera 引出纪年含义。

items.example: Aes is the older Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: aes 是较早的拉丁语名词。

items.example: Aera becomes the base of era.
items.exampleCN: aera 成为 era 的基础。
era 保留「计数时间」的含义。

items.example: Epoch is a near period word.
Age is the plainer near word.
items.exampleCN: age 是更朴素的近义词。

definition_zh: 侵蚀；磨蚀；逐渐削弱；使逐渐丧失
definition_en: to wear away rock or soil gradually, or to weaken and reduce something such as value, trust or rights
core_image: 海浪日夜拍打崖壁，把松软岩层一点点掏空，崖顶草地不断向后退
scene: 海浪日夜拍打崖壁，把松软的岩层一点点掏空，崖顶的草地正往后退。Waves erode the soft cliff a little more each winter.
sceneCN: 这里 erode 指「（自然营力）逐渐磨掉、掏空岩体」（第 1 个义项：侵蚀岩石或土壤）；句意为海浪每个冬天都多啃掉一点这段软崖。可辨识物件：崖壁、浪花、掏空的岩层、崖顶草地。

senses.title: Wear away rock or soil
senses.definition: of water, wind or ice: to wear away rock or soil gradually
senses.definitionCN: 指水、风或冰逐渐磨掉岩石或土壤
senses.example: Waves erode the soft cliff a little more each winter.
senses.exampleCN: 海浪每个冬天都多啃掉一点这段软崖。
senses.why: The transitive verb puts the agent first: waves erode cliffs.
senses.whyCN: 及物动词把营力放在前面：波浪侵蚀崖壁。

senses.title: Be worn away
senses.definition: to be worn away gradually by natural forces
senses.definitionCN: 指受自然营力逐渐磨蚀
senses.example: The old shore erodes faster than the headland.
senses.exampleCN: 旧岸比岬角侵蚀得更快。
senses.why: The intransitive verb lets the surface itself be the subject.
senses.whyCN: 不及物动词让表面本身成为主语。

senses.title: Reduce value or profit
senses.definition: to reduce money, profit or advantage gradually
senses.definitionCN: 指逐渐减少金钱、利润或优势
senses.example: Freight costs erode the profit on each crate.
senses.exampleCN: 运费侵蚀着每箱货的利润。
senses.why: Costs remove profit as water removes rock.
senses.whyCN: 成本移除利润，正如水移除岩石。

senses.title: Weaken confidence or trust
senses.definition: to make confidence, trust or reputation gradually weaker
senses.definitionCN: 指使信心、信任或声誉逐渐减弱
senses.example: Repeated delays eroded public trust in the project.
senses.exampleCN: 一再延误削弱了公众对这个项目的信任。
senses.why: Repeated failure removes trust grain by grain.
senses.whyCN: 反复失败一粒一粒地移除信任。

senses.title: Wear down rights or standards
senses.definition: to weaken rights, freedoms or standards by small steps
senses.definitionCN: 指以渐进方式削弱权利、自由或准则
senses.example: Emergency powers eroded the right to assemble.
senses.exampleCN: 紧急权力侵蚀了集会权。
senses.why: Small legal steps remove rights the way waves remove a cliff.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的小步移除权利，正如波浪移除崖壁。

senses.title: Wear away chemically
senses.definition: of acid: to eat into a surface such as enamel or metal
senses.definitionCN: 指酸对牙釉质、金属等表面的侵蚀
senses.example: Stomach acid can erode tooth enamel.
senses.exampleCN: 胃酸会侵蚀牙釉质。
senses.why: Acid attacks enamel at the chemical scale.
senses.whyCN: 酸在化学尺度上攻击牙釉质。

senses.title: Cut into the land
senses.definition: of a river: to cut a channel or valley into the land
senses.definitionCN: 指河流在地表切出河道或河谷
senses.example: The river erodes a narrow gorge through the limestone.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河在石灰岩中切出一条窄峡谷。
senses.why: A river removes bed and bank, which is how it cuts a channel.
senses.whyCN: 河流移除河床与河岸，正是这样切出河道。

senses.title: Gradually weaken an advantage or base
senses.definition: to reduce an advantage, majority or base by small degrees
senses.definitionCN: 指逐步减少优势、多数席位或基础
senses.example: New competitors eroded the firm's lead.
senses.exampleCN: 新的竞争者削弱了这家公司的领先地位。
senses.why: Competition removes a lead by small degrees.
senses.whyCN: 竞争一点一点地移除领先优势。

intro.en: Erode comes from Latin erodere 'to gnaw out', the same verb that stands behind erosion.
intro.cn: erode 来自拉丁 erodere「啃出、蚀去」，与 erosion 出自同一动词。

items.en: Rodere 'to gnaw' is the root verb; its pre-Latin origin is not established, and suggested Indo-European links are hypotheses.
items.cn: rodere「啃」是词根动词；它在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，所提出的印欧关联均属假说。

items.en: E- 'out' plus rodere gave erodere 'to gnaw away, eat into', used of animals, acids and ulcers before it was used of land.
items.cn: e-「出」加 rodere 构成 erodere「啃掉、蚀入」，在用于土地之前，先用于动物、酸与溃疡。

items.en: English took the verb from French eroder or directly from Latin in the seventeenth century, at first in medical and chemical contexts.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪经法语 eroder 或直接自拉丁语借入该动词，最初用于医学与化学语境。

items.en: In the nineteenth century erode became the everyday geological verb paired with erosion, and it was applied to rivers, glaciers and waves.
items.cn: 在十九世纪，erode 成为与 erosion 配对的地质日常动词，用于河流、冰川与波浪。

items.en: From the twentieth century the verb spread to money, trust and rights, where the image of slow removal still governs the meaning.
items.cn: 从二十世纪起，这个动词扩展到金钱、信任与权利，其中「缓慢移除」的形象仍主导词义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the deeper origin of rodere is unsettled. The route from Latin erodere to English erode is established, though the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：rodere 的更深来源没有定论。从拉丁 erodere 到英语 erode 的路径是确定的，但确切首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that look like erode but have other roots; group two holds verbs of wearing away and weakening.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似但词根不同的动词；第二组是表示磨损与削弱的动词。

entries.definition: To escape or avoid, from e- 'out' plus vadere 'go'; it shares the prefix and the sound but not the 'gnaw' root.
entries.definitionCN: 指逃脱或避开，来自 e-「出」加 vadere「走」；共享前缀与读音，但没有「啃」的词根。

entries.definition: To burst out, from e- plus rumpere 'break'; volcanic eruptions are the opposite of slow wearing.
entries.definitionCN: 指爆发，来自 e- 加 rumpere「破裂」；火山喷发与缓慢磨蚀正相反。

entries.definition: To eat away chemically, from cor- 'thoroughly' plus rodere; it is a true relative that stresses chemical attack.
entries.definitionCN: 指化学性蚀去，来自 cor-「彻底」加 rodere；它是真正的同族词，强调化学侵蚀。

entries.definition: To rub out or delete, from eradere 'to scrape out', built on the same rodere root; it means removing marks, not wearing land.
entries.definitionCN: 指擦掉或删除，来自 eradere「刮出」，建立在同一 rodere 词根上；它指去除痕迹，而非磨蚀土地。

entries.definition: The everyday equivalent for slow removal by friction or weather; erode is its technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指摩擦或风化造成缓慢移除的日常说法；erode 是其技术对应词。

entries.definition: To rub or scrape a surface, from ab- 'away' plus radere 'scrape'; it stresses contact friction.
entries.definitionCN: 指摩擦或刮削表面，来自 ab-「离开」加 radere「刮」；强调接触摩擦。

entries.definition: To carry off by water, as soil from a field; erode is the geological term for the same action.
entries.definitionCN: 指被水冲走，如田里的土；erode 是同一动作的地质术语。

entries.definition: To weaken something gradually, often secretly, from under- plus mine; it is the figurative cousin of erode.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐、常为暗中地削弱，来自 under- 加 mine；它是 erode 的比喻近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real verb family and the real abstract collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的动词词族与真实的抽象搭配。

normal.en: E- 'out' plus rodere 'gnaw': to gnaw material out of a surface.
normal.cn: e-「出」加 rodere「啃」：把材料从表面啃出去。

normal.en: The family runs erode, erosion, erosive, erosional, erodible, erosivity.
normal.cn: 词族包括 erode、erosion、erosive、erosional、erodible、erosivity。

normal.en: The same root appears in corrode, erase and rodent.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 corrode、erase 与 rodent 中。

normal.en: Fixed abstract phrases: erode confidence, erode trust, erode margins, erode rights.
normal.cn: 固定抽象搭配：削弱信心、侵蚀信任、侵蚀利润、侵蚀权利。

normal.en: In landscape writing erode takes a direct object: rivers erode valleys, waves erode cliffs.
normal.cn: 在地貌写作中 erode 直接带宾语：河流侵蚀河谷，海浪侵蚀崖壁。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose every step is a little lower than last year.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，每一级都比去年低一点。

abstract.en: Picture a promise rubbed thin by being repeated too often.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺因反复重申而被磨薄。

abstract.en: Picture a wave that never breaks anything, only carries one grain away.
abstract.cn: 想象一道浪从不打碎什么，只带走一粒沙。

examples.en: The river has eroded a channel thirty metres deep.
examples.cn: 这条河已切出三十米深的河道。

examples.en: Rising costs eroded the profit margin on the product.
examples.cn: 成本上升侵蚀了该产品的利润率。

examples.en: Repeated scandals eroded voters' trust in the council.
examples.cn: 接连的丑闻削弱了选民对议会的信任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一（e）揉的（rode）」——被水一揉就掉 → 侵蚀

root: 拉丁 e-「出」+ rodere「啃、啮」→ erodere「啃掉、蚀去」；英语经法语 eroder 或直接自拉丁语借入。rodere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one verb from the cliff to the balance sheet: a force removes material, then the same slow removal appears as a channel, as lost profit, as weakened trust, as narrowed rights, as etched enamel and as a shrinking lead.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个动词从崖壁走到账本：某种力量带走物质，同一种缓慢移除随后表现为河道、流失的利润、被削弱的信任、被收窄的权利、被蚀出的牙釉质与缩小的领先。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: surf hollowing the base of a cliff while the grass above moves inland.
core.cn: 核心意象：浪把崖脚掏空，上方的草地向内陆移动。

branches.en: ACT AND BE ACTED ON: the same verb works with an agent or with the surface itself.
branches.cn: 作用与受作用：同一动词既可带施事，也可描述表面本身。

branches.en: CUTTING DOWN: a river erodes a gorge by removing bed and bank.
branches.cn: 向下切割：河流靠移除河床与河岸切出峡谷。

branches.en: CHEMICAL TOOTH: acid erodes enamel by the same logic at a smaller scale.
branches.cn: 化学的牙齿：酸在更小尺度上按同一逻辑侵蚀牙釉质。

branches.en: MONEY AND TRUST: costs and delays remove value the way water removes rock.
branches.cn: 金钱与信任：成本与延误会像水搬走岩石那样搬走价值。

branches.en: RIGHTS AND LEADS: small steps remove what was once solid.
branches.cn: 权利与领先：小步侵蚀移除曾经稳固之物。

intro.en: Erode is a Latin verb whose prefix and root both recur, and whose English family is unusually large.
intro.cn: erode 是拉丁动词，前缀与词根都反复出现，其英语词族异常庞大。

latinIntro.en: Rodere 'to gnaw' gives erode, erosion, corrode, erase and rodent; e- 'out' marks removal.
latinIntro.cn: rodere「啃」衍生 erode、erosion、corrode、erase 与 rodent；e-「出」标记移除。

items.example: The prefix marks taking something out.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记把某物取出。

items.example: The eroding bank threatens the road.
items.exampleCN: 正在侵蚀的河岸威胁道路。

definition_zh: 侵蚀；腐蚀；削弱；逐渐丧失
definition_en: the wearing away of rock or soil by water, wind or ice, or the gradual weakening and loss of something abstract
core_image: 河谷里，河水年复一年磨掉崖脚，岸边泥土不断塌落，崖顶的草皮向后退
scene: 河谷里，河水年复一年磨掉崖脚，岸边的泥土不断塌落。River erosion has cut the gorge deeper each century.
sceneCN: 这里 erosion 指「水流、风或冰对岩石与土壤的磨蚀搬移」（第 1 个义项：自然营力造成的侵蚀）；句意为河流侵蚀使峡谷每个世纪都更深一些。可辨识物件：河谷、崖脚、塌落的泥土、崖顶草皮。

pos.zh: 侵蚀；腐蚀；削弱；逐渐丧失

senses.title: Wearing away by natural forces
senses.definition: the process by which water, wind, ice or waves wear away rock and soil
senses.definitionCN: 指水、风、冰或浪磨蚀岩石与土壤的过程
senses.example: River erosion has cut the gorge deeper each century.
senses.exampleCN: 河流侵蚀使峡谷每个世纪都更深一些。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'gnaw out', and geology applied it to the slow removal of land.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「啃出去」，地质学把它用于陆地的缓慢移除。

senses.title: The worn result or feature
senses.titleCN: 侵蚀造成的结果或地形
senses.definition: the worn surface, shape or feature left after material has been removed
senses.definitionCN: 指物质被移除后留下的磨蚀面、形状或地形
senses.example: The arch is a famous product of erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 这座拱门是侵蚀的著名产物。
senses.why: The worn shape is the visible remainder of the process.
senses.whyCN: 被磨出的形状是这一过程留下的可见残余。

senses.title: Loss of soil
senses.definition: the removal of topsoil by water or wind, usually as an agricultural problem
senses.definitionCN: 指水或风带走表土，通常作为农业问题
senses.example: Terracing reduced soil erosion on the slope.
senses.exampleCN: 梯田减少了坡地上的土壤侵蚀。
senses.why: Topsoil is the most valuable layer removed, so agriculture gave the process its own phrase.
senses.whyCN: 表土是被移除的最有价值的一层，农业因此给了这一过程一个专门说法。

senses.title: Coastal and beach loss
senses.definition: the retreat of a coastline or beach under wave action
senses.definitionCN: 指海岸线或海滩在波浪作用下后退
senses.example: Coastal erosion threatens the row of houses.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸侵蚀威胁着那排房屋。
senses.why: Waves are the agent at the coast, and the retreat is the measurable result.
senses.whyCN: 波浪是海岸上的营力，后退是可测的结果。

senses.title: Gradual loss of value or profit
senses.titleCN: 价值或利润的逐渐流失
senses.definition: the slow reduction of money, profit or advantage
senses.definitionCN: 指金钱、利润或优势缓慢减少
senses.example: Price competition caused a steady erosion of margins.
senses.exampleCN: 价格竞争造成利润率的持续侵蚀。
senses.why: Money is removed the way rock is: slowly, by contact, and never all at once.
senses.whyCN: 金钱像岩石一样被移除：缓慢、靠接触，且从不会一次全没。

senses.title: Weakening of rights or trust
senses.definition: the gradual weakening of rights, trust or standards
senses.definitionCN: 指权利、信任或准则逐渐削弱
senses.example: The new rules led to an erosion of privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定导致隐私受到侵蚀。
senses.why: Rights are removed by small steps rather than one blow, which is why erosion fits.
senses.whyCN: 权利是靠小步而非一击被移除，这正是「侵蚀」贴合的原因。

senses.title: Dental erosion
senses.definition: the chemical wearing away of tooth enamel by acid
senses.definitionCN: 指酸对牙釉质的化学性磨损
senses.example: Fizzy drinks contribute to dental erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 碳酸饮料会加剧牙齿酸蚀。
senses.why: Acid removes enamel chemically, and dentistry borrowed the geological word.
senses.whyCN: 酸以化学方式移除牙釉质，牙科借用了这个地质词。

senses.title: Decline of support or membership
senses.definition: the gradual loss of supporters, members or political base
senses.definitionCN: 指支持者、成员或政治基础的逐渐流失
senses.example: The party suffered erosion of its rural base.
senses.exampleCN: 该党在农村的基础遭到侵蚀。
senses.why: Support drains away gradually, like a coast retreating.
senses.whyCN: 支持逐渐流失，就像海岸后退。

intro.en: Erosion is a Latin noun of action from erodere 'to gnaw out', built from a prefix of removal and a verb for gnawing.
intro.cn: erosion 是拉丁动词 erodere「咬出、啃去」的动作名词，由表示移除的前缀与「啃咬」动词构成。

items.en: Rodere 'to gnaw, nibble, wear by gnawing' supplied the root; its own deeper origin is uncertain, and comparisons with Sanskrit rad- 'scratch' are hypotheses.
items.cn: rodere「啃、咬、啮磨」提供词根；它更深的来源不确定，与梵语 rad-「刮」的比较只是假说。

items.en: E- 'out' plus rodere produced erodere 'to gnaw away, eat out', used of animals and of acids long before geology.
items.cn: e-「出」加 rodere 构成 erodere「啃掉、蚀出」，在地质学之前很久就用于动物与酸。

items.en: Erosio, erosionis 'a gnawing away' is the action noun; English took it through French erosion in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: erosio、erosionis「啃蚀」是动作名词；英语在十六世纪经法语 erosion 借入。

items.en: Early English uses were medical and chemical, describing ulcers and the action of acids on metals.
items.cn: 早期英语用法属医学与化学，描写溃疡以及酸对金属的作用。

items.en: From the eighteenth century erosion became the standard geological term for the wearing away of land by water, wind and ice.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，erosion 成为标准地质术语，指水、风、冰对陆地的磨蚀。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Latin origin of rodere is unsettled, and any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction; the noun's own Latin derivation is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：rodere 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式；该名词本身的拉丁派生是确定的。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble erosion in sound or spelling; group two holds processes of wearing away and their opposites.
note.cn: 第一组是读音或拼写近似 erosion 的词；第二组是磨蚀过程及其反义词。

entries.definition: The act of avoiding or escaping, from e- 'out' plus vadere 'go'; the ending matches, the root does not.
entries.definitionCN: 指逃避或躲开，来自 e-「出」加 vadere「走」；词尾相合，词根不同。

entries.definition: A volcanic or sudden outburst, from e- plus rumpere 'break'; geologists keep it separate from erosion.
entries.definitionCN: 指火山喷发或突然爆发，来自 e- 加 rumpere「破裂」；地质学把它与侵蚀分开。

entries.definition: A rare medical word for scraping away tissue, from eradere 'to scrape out', a relative through the same rodere root.
entries.definitionCN: 指刮除组织的罕见医学词，来自 eradere「刮出」，经同一 rodere 词根与之相关。

entries.definition: Means able to be eroded, built with -ible; it shares the root but describes susceptibility rather than the process.
entries.definitionCN: 意为易受侵蚀的，由 -ible 构成；共享词根，但描述易受性而非过程。

entries.definition: Wearing by friction, as sand rubbing a surface; erosion includes removal by transport as well as rubbing.
entries.definitionCN: 指摩擦造成的磨损，如砂磨表面；erosion 除摩擦外还包括搬运移除。

entries.definition: The breakdown of rock where it lies, without removal; erosion then carries the pieces away.
entries.definitionCN: 指岩石在原地崩解而未被搬走；erosion 再把碎块带走。

entries.definition: Chemical wearing of metal or rock, especially by acid; it is a chemical cousin of erosion.
entries.definitionCN: 指金属或岩石受化学作用磨损，尤指酸蚀；它是 erosion 的化学近亲。

entries.definition: The laying down of material; it is the counterpart of erosion in the sediment budget.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质的堆积；在沉积收支中与侵蚀相对。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real word family and the real policy and dental phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的词族与真实的政策、牙科搭配。

normal.en: E- 'out' plus rodere 'gnaw': erosion is gnawing something out of the land.
normal.cn: e-「出」加 rodere「啃」：侵蚀就是把东西从地里啃出去。

normal.en: The family runs erode, erosion, erosive, erosional, erodible, erosivity.
normal.cn: 词族包括 erode、erosion、erosive、erosional、erodible、erosivity。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: soil erosion, coastal erosion, erosion rate, erosion control.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：土壤侵蚀、海岸侵蚀、侵蚀速率、侵蚀防治。

normal.en: Weathering breaks rock in place, erosion carries it away.
normal.cn: 风化在原地弄碎岩石，侵蚀把它搬走。

normal.en: The abstract use is regular: erosion of confidence, of margins, of privacy.
normal.cn: 抽象用法很规律：信心、利润率、隐私的侵蚀。

abstract.en: Picture a cliff that loses one grain for every wave and never notices.
abstract.cn: 想象一处崖壁每道浪带走一粒沙，却从不察觉。

abstract.en: Picture a savings account quietly eaten by fees.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被手续费悄悄吃掉的储蓄账户。

abstract.en: Picture a right that disappears not by law but by habit.
abstract.cn: 想象一项权利不是被法律取消，而是被习惯磨掉。

examples.en: Wind erosion stripped the field down to bare subsoil.
examples.cn: 风蚀把田地剥到只剩生土。

examples.en: Erosion of confidence followed the second product failure.
examples.cn: 第二次产品失败之后，信心受到侵蚀。

examples.en: Dentists warn that sweet drinks speed up enamel erosion.
examples.cn: 牙医警告甜饮料会加速牙釉质酸蚀。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一（e）揉（ro）神（sion）」——被水一遍遍揉掉 → 侵蚀

root: 拉丁 e-「出」+ rodere「啃、啮」→ erodere「啃掉」；再加 -io（动作名词后缀）→ erosio「啃蚀」，英语作 erosion。rodere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one loss: a force removes material, and the same slow removal then appears as a landform, as lost soil, as a retreating coast, as shrinking profit, as weakened rights, as worn enamel and as a vanishing base.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种失去展开：某种力量带走物质，同一种缓慢移除随后表现为地形、流失的表土、后退的海岸、缩水的利润、被削弱的权利、磨薄的牙釉质与消散的基础。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river grinding the foot of a cliff while the grass above edges backward.
core.cn: 核心意象：河水磨掉崖脚，上方的草皮向后退。

branches.en: PROCESS AND PRODUCT: the wearing and the worn shape are two views of one event.
branches.cn: 过程与产物：磨蚀与磨出的形状是同一事件的两种看法。

branches.en: TWO SCENES: a ploughed slope and a storm beach lose ground in the same way.
branches.cn: 两个场景：耕地坡面与风暴海滩以同样方式失去土地。

branches.en: MONEY WEARS: margins shrink the way cliffs do, slowly and irreversibly.
branches.cn: 金钱也会磨蚀：利润率像崖壁一样缓慢且不可逆地缩小。

branches.en: RIGHTS WEAR: what is not defended is quietly removed.
branches.cn: 权利也会磨蚀：无人守护的东西被悄悄移除。

branches.en: BODY AND BODY POLITIC: acid eats enamel, and indifference eats a party's base.
branches.cn: 身体与政治体：酸啃牙釉质，冷漠啃掉政党基础。

intro.en: Erosion is a Latin action noun whose prefix, root and suffix each recur in English.
intro.cn: erosion 是拉丁动作名词，其前缀、词根与后缀都在英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin rodere 'to gnaw' gives erode, erosion, corrode and rodent; e- 'out' marks removal, and -io marks the action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rodere「啃」衍生 erode、erosion、corrode 与 rodent；e-「出」标记移除，-io 标记动作。

items.exampleCN: 降雨侵蚀力随季节变化。

items.meaning: to eat away by chemical action

definition_zh: 犯错；出差错；越轨
definition_en: to make a mistake, or to behave in a way that is morally wrong
core_image: 地图上偏出一度的那条线，走时不觉，到终点才发现整条路都斜了
scene: 老话提醒人都会犯错。Wise writers admit that humans err.
sceneCN: 这里 err 是「犯错；出差错」（第 1 个义项：判断或行为偏离正确）；句意：明智的作者承认人都会犯错。

collocations.phrase: err on the side of caution

senses.title: To be mistaken
senses.definition: to reach a wrong result or form a wrong judgment
senses.definitionCN: 得出错误结果或作出错误判断
senses.example: Even the referee errs.
senses.exampleCN: 连裁判也会出错。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stray from the road, so a mistake is a step off the path.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义是偏离道路，故错误就是离路一步。

senses.title: To do wrong morally
senses.definition: to act against what is right, especially in religious language
senses.definitionCN: 行为违背正当，尤见于宗教用语
senses.example: Scripture says all have erred.
senses.exampleCN: 经文说众人都犯了罪。
senses.why: Devotional writing kept the older sense of wandering into sin.
senses.whyCN: 灵修文字保留了误入罪途这层古义。

senses.title: To go astray physically
senses.definition: a literary use meaning to wander from the intended way
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法，指偏离应走之路
senses.example: A ship errs from its course.
senses.exampleCN: 一艘船偏离了航线。
senses.why: Poetry preserves the literal straying that prose now only figurative.
senses.whyCN: 诗歌保存了字面上的偏离，散文如今只用作比喻。

intro.en: Err is from Latin errare, to wander or stray, which gave English error, erratic and errand as well.
intro.cn: err 出自拉丁语 errare「游荡、偏离」，同族还给了英语 error、erratic 与 errand。

items.en: Errare means to wander, and so to be mistaken.
items.cn: errare 表游荡，因而表出错。

items.en: Error names the wandering itself.
items.cn: error 命名这种游荡本身。

items.en: Erreur and errer carry the sense into French.
items.cn: erreur 与 errer 把词义带入法语。

items.en: Middle English records erren as a verb.
items.cn: 十三世纪中古英语记录动词 erren。

items.en: The spelling settles to err while error keeps the double r.
items.cn: 近代早期拼写定为 err，error 仍保双 r。

items.en: Two maxims keep the word in daily speech.
items.cn: 两句格言让该词留存于日常。

note.en: Group one holds the errare wandering family; group two holds other verbs of going wrong.
note.cn: 第一组是 errare 这一表游荡的词族；第二组是其他表出错的动词。

entries.definition: The mistake itself, from the same Latin wandering.
entries.definitionCN: 错误本身，出自同一拉丁语游荡。

entries.definition: Straying from the proper course, as in knight-errant.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离正道，如游侠骑士一词。

entries.definition: Moving unpredictably, built on the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 变动不定，基于同一词干。

entries.definition: A departure from what is normal, from ab- plus errare.
entries.definitionCN: 背离常态，由 ab- 加 errare 构成。

entries.definition: The plain word for getting something wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 弄错的朴素说法。

entries.definition: To err heavily and conspicuously.
entries.definitionCN: 重重地、明显地犯错。

entries.definition: To lose the right path, moral or literal.
entries.definitionCN: 失去正路，或指道德或指实际。

entries.definition: To cross a set boundary, chiefly in moral language.
entries.definitionCN: 越过既定界线，多用于道德语域。

normalIntro.en: Err is short and formal; mistake is the everyday verb.
normalIntro.cn: err 短促且书面，mistake 才是日常动词。

normal.en: Double the r before a vowel: erred, erring, errant.
normal.cn: 元音前双写 r：erred、erring、errant。

normal.en: Err on the side of caution means choose the safer reading.
normal.cn: 「err on the side of caution」意为宁可过于谨慎。

normal.en: To err is human pairs with to forgive divine.
normal.cn: To err is human 下句常接 to forgive divine。

normal.en: Use err in essays, mistake in speech.
normal.cn: 论文里用 err，口语里用 mistake。

normal.en: Religious prose keeps the moral sense of the verb.
normal.cn: 宗教文体保留该动词的道德义。

abstract.en: Picture a footpath where one mistaken step leads off the trail.
abstract.cn: 想象一步走错便离开山径的小路。

abstract.en: Imagine a compass needle swinging a few degrees off north.
abstract.cn: 想象偏离正北几度的罗盘指针。

abstract.en: Think of a printer's sheet marked with the one wrong line.
abstract.cn: 想想印张上被圈出的那一行错字。

examples.en: Analysts err when they trust a single source.
examples.cn: 分析师只信单一来源时便会出错。

examples.en: The report erred in its opening count.
examples.cn: 报告在开头的计数上出了错。

examples.en: Judge a person who errs and repairs.
examples.cn: 评判一个会犯错又会补救的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿」——饿得头昏眼花便一步走歪，所以 err 是犯错、出差错；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 errare（游荡、偏离正道）→ 古法语 errer → 中古英语 erren → 现代英语 err，核心义「从正路上走偏一步」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb moves from ordinary mistakes, through moral failing, to a literary sense of straying.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从日常出错，经道德过失，到文学性的迷途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step taken off the marked road.
core.cn: 核心意象：从既定道路上迈出的一步偏斜。

branches.en: Judgment slips from the right answer.
branches.cn: 判断从正解上滑开。

branches.en: Will slips from the right conduct.
branches.cn: 意志从正当行为上滑开。

branches.en: The body slips from the right path.
branches.cn: 身体从正路上滑开。

branches.en: Both keep the road metaphor literally visible.
branches.cn: 两者都让道路隐喻清晰可见。

branches.en: Both admit correction as the next move.
branches.cn: 两者都把补救视为下一步。

intro.en: A single Latin stem spreads into verbs, nouns and adjectives by adding endings.
intro.cn: 同一个拉丁词干靠添加词尾扩散为动词、名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin errare is to wander, error a wandering, and erraticus wandering.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 errare 表游荡，error 表游荡之事，erraticus 表游荡的。

items.example: Err- is the whole stem here.
The noun keeps the double r.
Book lists use the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 书末勘误表用拉丁形式。

definition_zh: 不稳定的；古怪的；（岩石）异地搬运的
definition_en: moving or behaving unpredictably, and strange or irregular in character
core_image: 一块孤零零躺在田中央的巨石，附近的山岩却全是另一种石头，像被谁从远处搬来又随手丢下
scene: 他的发球落点忽长忽短。His serves were erratic.
sceneCN: 这里 erratic 是「不稳定的；忽好忽坏的」（第 1 个义项：无规律地变动）；句意：他的发球忽长忽短。

pos.zh: 不稳定的；古怪的；（岩石）异地搬运的

senses.title: Irregular in movement or amount
senses.definition: varying without a rule that others can predict
senses.definitionCN: 无规则可预测地变动
senses.example: Rainfall stayed erratic all spring.
senses.exampleCN: 整个春天降雨都飘忽不定。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to wander, and a wandering course has no fixed rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义为游荡，游荡之径自然没有固定节律。

senses.title: Strange in conduct
senses.definition: behaving in ways that depart from what people expect of a person
senses.definitionCN: 行为偏离众人对某人的常规期待
senses.example: The manager turned erratic.
senses.exampleCN: 那位经理变得反复无常。
senses.why: Applied to character, straying from the road becomes straying from normal conduct.
senses.whyCN: 用于品性时，离路便成了离经日常的举止。

senses.title: Rock carried far from its source
senses.definition: describing stone found far from the formation it belongs to, especially by ice
senses.definitionCN: 指远离其母岩产地而出现的石块，尤由冰川搬运所致
senses.example: Glaciers left erratic boulders.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川留下了异地搬运的巨石。
senses.why: Geology kept the wandering image literally: the boulder itself went astray.
senses.whyCN: 地质学字面保留了游荡意象：巨石本身迷了途。

intro.en: Erratic is from Latin erraticus, of wandering, built on errare to stray.
intro.cn: erratic 出自拉丁语 erraticus「游荡的」，建在动词 errare「偏离」之上。

items.en: Errare means to wander or go astray.
items.cn: errare 意为游荡或走偏。

items.en: Erraticus describes things that stray, such as planets called wandering stars.
items.cn: erraticus 形容偏离之物，如被称为游星行星。

items.en: Erratique passes the adjective into French.
items.cn: erratique 把形容词带入法语。

items.en: English first uses erratic of heavenly bodies that move.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语首用 erratic 指移动的天体。

items.en: Writing applies it to unstable minds and habits.
items.cn: 十七世纪书面语把它用于不稳定的心性与习惯。

items.en: Geology names stray boulders erratic blocks.
items.cn: 十九世纪地质学把迷途巨石称为漂砾。

note.en: Group one holds the errare wandering family; group two holds other adjectives of irregularity.
note.cn: 第一组是 errare 这一表游荡的词族；第二组是其他表无规律的形容词。

entries.definition: A short trip taken to deliver something, from the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 为送物而行的短途，同出一根。

entries.definition: A wrong judgment, the plain sibling of erratic.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的判断，与 erratic 为平辈姊妹词。

entries.definition: Straying from the right course, as in knight-errant.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离正途，如游侠骑士一语。

entries.definition: A deviation from type, with the prefix ab- away.
entries.definitionCN: 背离典型，前缀 ab- 表离开。

entries.definition: The plain term for results no one can forecast.
entries.definitionCN: 无人能预判的结果，说法朴素。

entries.definition: Starting and stopping in uneven spells.
entries.definitionCN: 一阵一阵，忽起忽停。

entries.definition: Changing on impulse, with a stronger note of arbitrariness.
entries.definitionCN: 一时兴起而变，任意性更重。

entries.definition: Wandering from the appointed way in older prose.
entries.definitionCN: 早期文体中偏离应行之路。

normalIntro.en: Erratic marks a pattern with no pattern; capricious marks a will with no reason.
normalIntro.cn: erratic 指标记无规律，capricious 指意志无道理。

normal.en: Stress sits on the second syllable: i-RAT-ic.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节：i-RAT-ic。

normal.en: It modifies series and rates, not single facts.
normal.cn: 修饰系列与速率，而非孤立事实。

normal.en: In geology the noun form is an erratic block.
normal.cn: 地质学中名词形式为漂砾。

normal.en: The adverb erratically is the usual collocation.
normal.cn: 副词 erratically 是常见搭配。

normal.en: Avoid it for merely strange behaviour without change.
normal.cn: 只是古怪而无变动时不宜用。

abstract.en: Picture a heartbeat traced on paper with uneven gaps.
abstract.cn: 想象纸带上间距不匀的心跳曲线。

abstract.en: Imagine a boulder sitting alone in a wheat field far from any cliff.
abstract.cn: 想象一块巨石孤零零躺在远离崖壁的麦田里。

abstract.en: Think of a driver who alternates between crawling and sprinting.
abstract.cn: 想想那位忽慢忽快的司机。

examples.en: Erratic supply pushed prices upward.
examples.cn: 供应不稳把价格推高。

examples.en: He behaved erratically once the lights came on.
examples.cn: 灯光一亮他的举止便失常。

examples.en: The cliff face holds one erratic block of foreign granite.
examples.cn: 崖壁上嵌着一块异地而来的花岗岩漂砾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「衣拉提克」——衣服一会儿被拉起一会儿被扯紧，忽松忽紧，所以 erratic 是不稳定的、古怪的；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 errare（游荡、走偏）＋ 形容词后缀 -aticus（与……有关的）→ erraticus（游荡的）→ 法语 erratique → 英语 erratic，核心义「像离了路一样没有定规」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective covers irregular series, odd conduct, and a technical term for transported rock.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词涵盖无规律的系列、反常的举止，以及搬运岩石的术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn with no ruler, wandering wherever the hand goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：不用尺画出的线，随手走到哪儿偏到哪儿。

branches.en: Quantity and rhythm lose their regular beats.
branches.cn: 数量与节奏失去均匀的拍点。

branches.en: Conduct abandons the expected route.
branches.cn: 举止离开了预期的路径。

branches.en: Ice carries stone where stone does not belong.
branches.cn: 冰川把石头搬到不属于它的地方。

branches.en: Both describe change over time without a rule.
branches.cn: 两者都描述无规律的时间之变。

branches.en: Both can be measured, only not forecast.
branches.cn: 两者都可计量，只是无法预测。

intro.en: A stem of straying takes an adjectival ending borrowed through Latin and French.
intro.cn: 表偏离的词干加上经拉丁语与法语传入的形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin errare is to wander, erraticus wandering, and erratum a mistaken thing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 errare 表游荡，erraticus 表游荡的，erratum 表错误之物。

items.example: A noun from the same wandering.
items.exampleCN: 同一游荡义派生的名词。

items.example: Book lists keep the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 书末勘误表保留拉丁形式。

items.example: Ab- adds the sense of away.

definition_zh: 错误的；不正确的；基于误判的
definition_en: wrong or based on a mistake
core_image: 一个人偏离了直路，走进岔道还以为是正途
scene: 报告里有一个错误的数据，结论因此站不住脚。The report contained an erroneous figure, so its conclusion failed.
sceneCN: 这里 erroneous 是「错误的」（第 1 个义项：事实或内容不正确）；句意：报告里有一个错误的数据，所以结论站不住脚。

pos.zh: 错误的；不正确的；基于误判的

senses.title: Factually wrong
senses.definition: containing a mistake or not matching the facts
senses.definitionCN: 包含错误或与事实不符的
senses.example: The article was based on erroneous data.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章建立在错误的数据之上。
senses.why: The adjective comes from error, whose Latin root means wandering, so a wrong statement has strayed from the truth.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词来自 error，其拉丁词根意为「游荡」，所以错误的陈述偏离了真相。

senses.title: Based on mistaken judgment
senses.definition: formed from a wrong belief, assumption, or way of reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 建立在错误信念、假设或推理方式上的
senses.example: Their conclusion proved erroneous after further study.
senses.exampleCN: 进一步研究后，他们的结论被证明是错的。
senses.why: A mistaken judgment is a path of thought that has wandered off course.
senses.whyCN: 错误的判断就是一条偏离正轨的思路。

intro.en: Erroneous comes from Latin erroneus, wandering, from errare, to wander or stray.
intro.cn: erroneous 来自拉丁语 erroneus（游荡的），源于 errare（漫游、走偏）。

items.en: Errare means to wander or stray.
items.cn: errare 意为游荡、走偏。

items.en: Error means a wandering or a mistake.
items.cn: error 意为游荡或错误。

items.en: Erroneus means wandering or mistaken.
items.cn: erroneus 意为游荡的、错误的。

items.en: Erroneous enters English with the mistake sense.
items.cn: erroneous 以「错误」的含义进入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses erroneous mainly for beliefs and information.
items.cn: 现代英语中，erroneous 主要用于信念和信息。

note.en: Erroneous is the adjective of error, close to its family and to words for being wrong.
note.cn: erroneous 是 error 的形容词，与自身词族以及表示「错误」的词相邻。

entries.definition: a mistake
entries.definitionCN: 错误

entries.definition: by mistake
entries.definitionCN: 错误地

entries.definition: wandering or straying
entries.definitionCN: 漫游的；走偏的

entries.definition: not right or true
entries.definitionCN: 不正确的

entries.definition: wrong in opinion or judgment
entries.definitionCN: 判断错误的

entries.definition: not true
entries.definitionCN: 虚假的；不真实的

normalIntro.en: Erroneous comes from wandering: a wrong idea has walked off the true path.
normalIntro.cn: erroneous 来自「游荡」：错误的想法走离了正确的道路。

normal.en: Erroneous data leads to bad decisions.
normal.cn: 错误的数据导致糟糕的决定。

normal.en: An erroneous belief is a belief that is not true.
normal.cn: erroneous belief 是不符合事实的信念。

normal.en: The adverb erroneously means by mistake.
normal.cn: 副词 erroneously 表示错误地。

normal.en: The noun error is the simpler relative.
normal.cn: 名词 error 是更简单的亲属词。

normal.en: Compare mistaken: mistaken stresses the person, erroneous stresses the content.
normal.cn: 对比 mistaken：mistaken 强调人，erroneous 强调内容。

abstract.en: Picture a traveler taking the wrong fork in a road.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人在岔路口走错了方向。

abstract.en: Imagine a map with one line drawn in the wrong place.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上有一条线画错了位置。

abstract.en: Think of a calculator showing a number that cannot be right.
abstract.cn: 想象计算器显示出一个不可能正确的数字。

examples.en: The rumor turned out to be erroneous.
examples.cn: 那个谣言最终被证明是错的。

examples.en: An erroneous assumption ruined the whole plan.
examples.cn: 一个错误的假设毁掉了整个计划。

examples.en: Please correct any erroneous entries in the list.
examples.cn: 请更正清单中任何错误的条目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「error + neous」——带着「错误」的形容词，就是错误的；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 errare（游荡、走偏）→ error（错误）→ erroneus（游荡的、错误的）→ 英语 erroneous，核心义「偏离正途而错」。

sensesIntro.en: Erroneous first describes wrong facts or statements, and then wrong beliefs or ways of reasoning.
sensesIntro.cn: erroneous 先描述错误的事实或陈述，再描述错误的信念或推理方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path that has strayed away from the true road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条偏离正路的岔道。

branches.en: Wrong content is the main factual sense.
branches.cn: 内容错误是主要事实义项。

branches.en: Wrong judgment applies straying to reasoning.
branches.cn: 误判把「走偏」用于推理。

branches.en: Bad data and bad assumptions both lead reasoning astray.
branches.cn: 坏数据与坏假设都会把推理带偏。

branches.en: A statement and a figure can both be erroneous.
branches.cn: 陈述与数字都可能是错误的。

branches.en: A belief and a conclusion can both rest on error.
branches.cn: 信念与结论都可能建立在错误之上。

intro.en: Erroneous is a Latin wandering adjective, with English relatives error, erroneously, and erroneousness.
intro.cn: erroneous 是拉丁语中表示「走偏」的形容词，英语亲属有 error、erroneously 与 erroneousness。

latinIntro.en: Latin errare means to wander, and error means a wandering or mistake.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 errare 意为游荡，error 意为游荡或错误。

definition_zh: 错误地；不正确地；荒谬地
definition_en: in a way that is wrong because it rests on a mistaken belief or faulty reasoning
core_image: 报表上一格小数点错位，下面整列数字跟着齐步走错，没人抬头看一眼
scene: 名单把他错列为毕业生。The list erroneously enrolled him.
sceneCN: 这里 erroneously 是「错误地；误以为真地」（第 1 个义项：因前提有误而做错）；句意：名单误把他说成毕业生。

pos.zh: 错误地；不正确地；荒谬地

senses.title: Wrong because the premise is wrong
senses.definition: in a manner resulting from a false belief rather than from intent
senses.definitionCN: 源于错误信念而非出于故意
senses.example: He was erroneously blamed.
senses.exampleCN: 他受到了错误的指责。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the adjective's fault into the way an act is done.
senses.whyCN: 副词词尾把形容词的缺陷变成动作的方式。

senses.title: Incorrect in record or statement
senses.definition: used when a document, figure or report gives what is not true
senses.definitionCN: 指文件、数字或报道给出失实内容
senses.example: The ledger was erroneously closed.
senses.exampleCN: 账簿被误关闭了。
senses.why: Legal and clerical prose reach for it to soften blame on a person.
senses.whyCN: 法律与文书用它来淡化对个人的追责。

senses.title: Ridiculously mistaken
senses.definition: a rhetorical use stressing how far from sense the mistake is
senses.definitionCN: 修辞用法，强调错误离常识之远
senses.example: They erroneously trusted the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们竟然误信了那条谣言。
senses.why: Commentary borrows the adverb to signal an error beyond excuse.
senses.whyCN: 评论借用该副词来标记不可原谅之错。

intro.en: Erroneously descends from Latin erroneus, going astray, from errare to wander, plus -ous, then -ly.
intro.cn: erroneously 源自拉丁语 erroneus「走偏的」，出自 errare「游荡」加 -ous，再添副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Errare means to wander or stray.
items.cn: errare 意为游荡或偏离。

items.en: Erroneus describes an opinion that has gone astray.
items.cn: erroneus 形容走偏的见解。

items.en: The suffix -osus supplies the quality ending.
items.cn: 后缀 -osus 提供表性质的词尾。

items.en: English takes erroneous with a scholarly air.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语以书面色彩摄入 erroneous。

items.en: Religious dispute loads it with blame for false doctrine.
items.cn: 十七世纪宗教论争把它压上异端之责。

items.en: Editing and law use it to mark a simple inaccuracy.
items.cn: 现代编校与法律用它标示单纯失实。

note.en: Group one holds the error family and its adverbs; group two holds other adverbs of doing something wrong.
note.cn: 第一组是 error 词族及其副词；第二组是其他表做错方式的副词。

entries.definition: Describes the belief or statement itself, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 形容信念或陈述本身，而非动作。

entries.definition: Signals no regular pattern, not wrongness of content.
entries.definitionCN: 提示没有规律，而非内容有误。

entries.definition: Marks a slip in precision, milder than erroneously.
entries.definitionCN: 标示精度上的偏差，语气弱于 erroneously。

entries.definition: The plain household word for the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 同一意思的日常说法。

entries.definition: The briefest adverb for doing or judging amiss.
entries.definitionCN: 表做错或判错的最简短副词。

entries.definition: Stresses that what was said is not true, sometimes on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 强调所述不实，有时含故意。

entries.definition: Marks a failure to meet a standard or format.
entries.definitionCN: 标示未达标准或格式。

entries.definition: Points at a broken chain of reasoning rather than a false fact.
entries.definitionCN: 指向断裂的推理链而非虚假事实。

normalIntro.en: Erroneously attacks the premise; incorrectly attacks the form.
normalIntro.cn: erroneously 指向前提有误，incorrectly 指向形式不合。

normal.en: Common before believe, assume, report, credit.
normal.cn: 常置于 believe、assume、report、credit 之前。

normal.en: Formal register; prefer mistakenly in speech.
normal.cn: 语域正式；口语宜用 mistakenly。

normal.en: Passive notices use it to avoid naming a culprit.
normal.cn: 被动通告用它来回避点出责任人。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with arbitrarily, which is about whim.
normal.cn: 不要与 arbitrarily 混淆，后者关乎一时兴起。

normal.en: It carries no blame of intent, only of fact.
normal.cn: 它不指责动机，只指陈事实。

abstract.en: Picture a decimal point moved one place, dragging a column with it.
abstract.cn: 想象小数点移了一格，带着整列数字一起走错。

abstract.en: Imagine a label tied to the wrong suitcase on a carousel.
abstract.cn: 想象行李转盘上标签系错了箱子。

abstract.en: Think of a signature on a form that says the opposite.
abstract.cn: 想想在一份写着相反内容的表格上签下的名字。

examples.en: She was erroneously listed as retired.
examples.cn: 她被误列为已退休。

examples.en: The paper erroneously credits another lab.
examples.cn: 那篇论文误把成果记在另一实验室名下。

examples.en: Few readers notice the figures were erroneously summed.
examples.cn: 鲜有读者注意到这些数字被错误地加总了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一路泥湿」——一路都把泥泞误认作实地，走得步步不对，所以 erroneously 是错误地、失误地；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 errare（游荡、走偏）→ erroneus（走偏的、错误的）＋ -ous（具有……性质的）→ erroneous ＋ 副词词尾 -ly → erroneously，核心义「以偏离正路的方式行事或判断」。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb covers mistakes of premise, faults of record, and a rhetorical stress on absurdity.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词涵盖前提之误、记载之失，以及强调荒谬的修辞用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step taken in good faith on ground that is not where it was marked.
core.cn: 核心意象：在标注有误的地面上凭诚意迈出的一步。

branches.en: A false premise drives the whole act.
branches.cn: 错误前提驱动整个行为。

branches.en: Documents repeat the error without anyone meaning it.
branches.cn: 文件无人有意地复述这一错误。

branches.en: Commentary stresses how far off course the act was.
branches.cn: 评论强调这一步偏航之远。

branches.en: Both treat the mistake as unintentional.
branches.cn: 两者都把错误视为非故意。

branches.en: Both belong to written and public speech.
branches.cn: 两者都属于书面与公开言说。

intro.en: Three endings stack on one stem of straying: -eus, -ous, then -ly.
intro.cn: 三层词尾叠在同一个表偏离的词干上：先是 -eus，再是 -ous，最后是 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin errare is to wander, erroneus mistaken, and error a wandering.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 errare 表游荡，erroneus 表错误的，error 表游荡之事。

items.example: Err- is the whole family core.
items.exampleCN: err- 是整个词族的核心。
